column15: The confrontation occurred shortly after 1:30 p.m. in a parking lot in the 17100 block of West Foothill Boulevard, between Palmetto and Sierra avenues, according to the Fontana Police Department. Officers attempted to a detain a man wanted in connection with the sale and trafficking of "a large quantity of narcotics," primarily fentanyl, the department said in a statement. "During the attempted arrest, the person used his vehicle to ram multiple police vehicles and a civilian bystander vehicle," the news release said. "An officer-involved shooting subsequently occurred."

According to a City News Service report, police responded to the Valley Pointe Apartments complex at Roscoe Boulevard and Amestoy Avenue in Northridge at 11:37 p.m. Wednesday. The news service quoted an unnamed LAPD officer as saying the man who was killed was firing an assault rifle into the air. An off-duty ICE agent shot and killed him.

Police were called to an apartment at Pacific Avenue and W. 37th Street around 9:40 p.m. for a domestic violence and restraining order violation.  As officers confronted the person inside the victim's apartment, he refused to comply with orders, police said. The person has been identified as 39-year-old Lawrence Gonzales. "The officers approached Gonzales, who physically resisted their efforts to detain him," according to the LAPD. "The physical resistance escalated into a violent confrontation where Gonzales attempted to disarm the officers, resulting in an officer-involved shooting."

An OHP spokesperson said three troopers spotted a vehicle believed to be connected to an escaped inmate. A confrontation followed, and Butler ran from the scene carrying a .22-caliber rifle. Mark Southall with OHP said it is unclear whether the person fired the weapon or how many shots were fired by troopers. The person was pronounced dead at the scene and later identified as Butler.

GCPD officers located a vehicle that was wanted in connection to a BOLO released by the Roswell Police Department. The wanted vehicle was parked at a business on Peachtree Industrial Boulevard in Peachtree Corners. An officer attempted to box the wanted vehicle in, but the driver, later identified as Ivy, rammed the officer's vehicle, leaving it inoperable. The wanted vehicle fled the scene with responding GCPD officers in pursuit. The wanted vehicle crashed in the 7000 block of Peachtree Industrial Boulevard. Ivy exited the vehicle and started running. As officers chased Ivy, he took out a handgun and pointed it towards the officers. Two officers fired their weapons, fatally wounding Ivy.

column7: N Main St and Canal St
column15: According to the Eaton Rapids Police Department, an officer attempted to pull a vehicle over on S Main Street just before 10 p.m. The vehicle fled and crashed at the intersection of N Main Street and Canal Street. The person fled on foot. The police department said the person refused to obey numerous commands from the officer and informed the officer he had a gun. During the encounter, the suspect was shot by the officer. The person was transported to the Eaton Rapids Medical Center, where he was pronounced dead.

column7: E Division St and S 7th St
column15: Slaton police shot and killed someone but few details are available.

The Tucson Police Department is investigating after a suspect was shot and killed during an officer-involved shooting. The TPD says officers responded Monday night, December 29, to a home in the 1900 block of South Montezuma Avenue following a shots heard call. That’s where police say officers encountered a female in front of the residence, and the officer-involved shooting occurred.

It began about 6:30 p.m. Dec. 29 with a task force doing surveillance at a home on Ponce Boulevard near New Berlin Road for a person, William Lowe, who had warrants for a stolen car and several business burglaries. He could be seen peeking outside and after about an hour got into a vehicle that arrived, Chief Alan Parker said. As Lowe and the driver pulled out of the driveway, the officers stopped the car and took Lowe into custody. But the driver did not comply and wouldn’t turn the car off when another officer tried to detain him, Parker said. “As he’s getting him out of the car, that suspect begins to fight,” the chief said. “They fight pretty hard, they go to the ground, and during the altercation that suspect produces a handgun, and the officer was luckily able to shoot him in the head himself with his own handgun and end the threat at that time. That suspect did not survive his injury.”

Shortly after 12:30 a.m. on Dec. 29, a Virginia State trooper spotted a person wanted for evading officers earlier. The suspect, identified as 25-year-old Jacob Wesley Adkins of Hurt, was driving north on Route 29 in a Ford Fusion. Adkins continued to flee from officers, leading the trooper to use the Precision Immobilization Technique to stop the vehicle on Deerview Road. Once stopped, Adkins allegedly pulled out a rifle and fired at the trooper while inside the vehicle, according to Virginia State Police. The trooper returned fire, striking Adkins.

Pierce County Sheriff’s Office (PCSO) deputies were called to the 8500 block of 156th St Ct E at 2:01 a.m. after someone called 911 and said a man in a vehicle had fired a gunshot outside their home. When deputies arrived, they found the vehicle with a man sleeping inside. After speaking with the victims, deputies found probable cause to arrest the man. Deputies approached the vehicle to talk to the man, and shortly after, called out that shots had been fired.

The incident began around 9:12 p.m. on Dec 28, when dispatch received a welfare check call regarding an elderly woman’s granddaughter, identified as Georgeann Alexandra Goodman, 34. The caller reported that Georgeann was threatening self-harm and might be mentally unstable and potentially intoxicated. She was believed to be at a friend’s residence before heading to a location on South 14th Avenue. Deputies established a perimeter and staged nearby. Around 11:44 p.m., an officer reported Georgeann approached, stating she wanted to be shot, with her hands in her pockets and claiming to be armed. She was described as standing in the middle of the road, being belligerent. Minutes later, shots were fired. Georgeann was struck, went down, but reportedly still had the gun in her hand. An armored vehicle (MRAP) was deployed to secure the scene and remove the weapon. Life-saving measures, including CPR, were attempted, but Georgeann was pronounced deceased.

Officers were called around 11:55 p.m. to the area of Northeast 46th Street and 132nd Avenue. Police said initial calls reported a man was outside a home and pointed a gun at a woman who was inside. At least one shot was fired before officers arrived. When officers reached the scene, police said the man confronted them while holding a gun. Two officers fired their weapons, striking the man.

Sheriff William Eddy said during a news conference on Friday that the person shot two ladies in a pickup truck, hitting them in the leg. The suspect also shot a deputy, knicking him in the ear. Eddy also said during the news conference that the person was carrying “several guns.”

Mint Hill police were called to the Edible (formerly known as Edible Arrangements) location in the Mint Hill Commons shopping center on Matthews-Mint Hill Road around 10:47 a.m. on Friday, Dec. 26, for a custody exchange. According to police, a man pulled out a gun and began to shoot. He was shot and killed, and two officers were seriously injured.

column12: Precinct 5 Cameron County Constable's Office, Harlingen Police Department
column15: At approximately 12:46 p.m. on Friday, the Combes Police Department initiated a vehicle pursuit with a wanted individual, identified as Arizmendi, who had outstanding felony warrants from Harlingen. After the vehicle stopped, police say Arizmendi exited the vehicle and began firing shots at law enforcement, according to the update. The Precinct 5 Cameron County Constables and Harlingen Police Officers returned fire and struck Arizmendi multiple times, according to a news release from DPS. A Justice of the Peace was called and pronounced Arizmendi dead at the scene.

In a press release Friday night, police said that officers initiated a traffic stop on a red Ford Ranger in the 6000 block of Lake Worth Blvd. around 6:56 p.m. The driver of the truck, a 56-year-old Jerry Scot Lee, had "an active probation revocation warrant for solicitation of prostitution." Lee fled from the stop, and a slow-speed chase ensued. Lee caused damage to his truck, causing him to stop behind the Walmart at 6360 Lake Worth Blvd. Police say that's when Lee exited the vehicle, "took a shooting stance, and pointed what appeared to be a weapon towards officers." Four Lake Worth police officers opened fire, striking the person. Officers rendered CPR until paramedics arrived on the scene and pronounced Lee dead.

According to police, someone called, thinking her car had been hit the parking lot. When she went outside, she said she saw a man standing in front of a tan SUV, allegedly pointing a gun at her, police said. HPD said the woman then called police. Once officers arrived, they said they located the man outside the gate. Officials said the man, who was in his 50s, did not comply with officers' commands, leading to three officers opening fire, hitting the man.

Beaumont police responded to the 4400 block of Diamond Street off West Virginia following a call reporting a disturbance involving a man with a handgun. The call-taker received information from the caller that the man had broken a glass door into a home and a woman was bleeding from injuries sustained due to the shattered glass. Two officers initially responded to the area and encountered the man armed with a handgun. The man failed to comply with verbal commands and charged toward the officers armed with the handgun, according to police, who say officers were forced to discharge their weapons. Bossette died at the scene.
column32: person with a gun, domestic disturbance

column15: The Brentwood Police Department said in a press release on Thursday that officers conducted a traffic stop at around 10:55 p.m. Wednesday in the area of Balfour Road and Foothill Drive for suspicion of DUI. Officers made contact with a man in his 40s, who was the only occupant in the vehicle. While speaking with him, the officers developed probable cause to search the car, police said. "During the search, officers located a loaded, high-powered rifle inside the vehicle," the police statement said. "When officers attempted to arrest the driver, he physically resisted arrest, refused to follow verbal commands, and ultimately grabbed the high-powered rifle." Police said one officer opened fire, hitting the man. Officers provided life-saving measures until medics arrived, but he died at the scene, police said.

Officials with the Lynchburg Police Department (LPD) said an assault suspect who suffered cardiac arrest after officers deployed a Taser has died. Police said Orlando T. Harding, 38, died on Tuesday, December 30 while receiving care at the Lynchburg General Hospital. The Taser incident happened Wednesday, December 24 in the 500 block of 5th Street. According to LPD, Harding was resisting arrest at the time. Shortly after he was taken into custody, Harding suffered an apparent heart attack. Responding officers provided medical aid at the scene before Harding was taken to the hospital.

According to law enforcement, Corporal Grade One Matthew T. “Ty” Snook, 34, was working the check-in desk of the DMV office at 2230 Hessler Blvd. as part of an overtime assignment when the 44-year-old man entered the building. After lingering for a short while, the man approached Snook and pulled out a gun, shooting him. After being shot, Snook reportedly pushed another DMV employee out of harm’s way before the man shot the trooper a second time. Multiple police agencies responded to calls for an active shooter at the DMV office, and a New Castle County police officer confronted and shot the man, police reported.

Around 4:40 p.m., the Tennessee Highway Patrol and KCSO responded to reports of a woman at the Weigel’s on Central Avenue Pike who may have been suicidal, KCSO said. For reasons still under investigation, two KCSO deputies fired their weapons around 10:53 p.m., the office said.

According to a news release from the Idaho Falls Police Department, officers responded to an apartment in the 700 block of Cleveland Street about 5 a.m. after a report of domestic violence. The man stated that he told the woman that he would kill her father if he came over, and that he had grabbed the knife for self-defense. Officers told the man that he was under arrest, and he reportedly lunged, grabbing the knife. According to the news release, officers tried to stop him, and a physical struggle occurred. One officer fired his gun, striking the man. The man dropped the knife, and officers attempted lifesaving measures.

Officers from the Alpena Police Department and troopers from the Michigan State Police (MSP) Alpena Post conducted a traffic stop after midnight on Grant Street, near Lawn Street, in Alpena Township because the vehicle was allegedly stolen. The Alpena man, an occupant of the vehicle, was shot by an Alpena Police Department officer after he brandished a knife and cut the officer’s hand.

San Diego police said sheriff's deputies were on site working the event when a man on a bike approached two deputies and a sergeant and asked to speak with them. “He made statements that were consistent with wanting to be shot," SDPD Lt. Lou Maggie said. Investigators said at one point during the conversation, the man pulled out a knife and began moving toward the deputies, who gave the man multiple commands to drop the weapon. When the man failed to comply, one sheriff's deputy fired at him several times and struck the man, police said.

Luis Arreola-Palma, 32, shot the officer at nearly point blank range as the officer was attempting to arrest him following a foot pursuit on Sunday in the area of Coors Blvd, and Illiff Rd., N.W. The bullet struck the officer’s police radio and he was not seriously injured. A second officer fired back at Arreola-Palma, striking him several times. Arreola-Palma was transported to a local hospital where he later died as a result of his injuries. Arreola-Palma had been identified on APD’s Top 25 Auto Theft Offender list for December and had two outstanding warrants.

Just after midnight on Sunday, police responded to a 911 call for a domestic dispute between a father and son at a building on Nameoke Street. Police found the 29-year-old Chez Frey outside in the hallway, allegedly holding a box cutter. Police said things escalated when the Fray and his father began to struggle. After repeated commands for Frey to drop the box cutter, police say he charged at officers, who, in tight quarters, feared for their lives. They say that’s why Fray was tased and then fatally shot.

According to Sheriff Salazar, around 8:30 in the morning, a woman was at home with her two children, both under the age of 10, when her ex-boyfriend entered the home without permission through an open door. The woman was able to flee with her two children and get to safety before calling deputies. The woman reported there had been some ongoing threats made towards her and her children. The suspect, believed to be armed with a rifle and a pistol, had threatened to kill himself or kill responding law enforcement. Deputy Sigala was able to make contact with Fernandez-Solano through a door that was partially cracked. The suspect's hands were not visible to deputies and they were prompted to push him through the door back into the room. A struggle could then be heard on bodycam footage and the suspect fired what deputies believe was a single shot. The round went "clean" through Deputy Sigala's hand and hit Deputy Zini's hip. Deputies returned fire, shooting three to four rounds, striking the suspect at least three times in the upper-body. Fernandez-Solano was pronounced dead at the scene.

Springfield Police received a call in Indian Orchard for reports of a man with a knife in the 1100 block of Worcester Street. Upon arriving to the scene, police discovered the man with erratic behavior. One police officer shot the man with his handgun and managed to hit the man. Officers then immediately tried to give the man medical aid, but he died on the scene.

According to Pelton, Franklin County deputies initially responded to a report of a suicidal person in the 1100 block of Highway OO. As deputies headed to the scene, a 911 caller reported hearing a gunshot in the basement of the home. After deputies arrived, they spoke with a woman inside the home and checked the basement, though deputies did not find anyone in the basement. After that, deputies conducted a perimeter search outside the home. They found and shot and killed a 60 year old man.

column12: Dallas Police Department, Mesquite Police Department
column15: Police conducted a felony traffic stop on a man alleged to have shot a woman. They allege he got out with a gun and they shot and killed him.

column12: Opp Police Department, Alabama Law Enforcement Agency
column15: According to a release sent out this afternoon, the manhunt for Amos Matthews led Opp police officers and an ALEA Special Agent to a home on Childre Court, where the law enforcement officials located Matthews. According to ALEA, Matthews was still armed during this encounter, and at some point, he attempted to run. Officers and the Special Agent would shoot at Matthews in response to his attempted escape, and he was struck by the gunfire.

Officers were called back to the same address around 12:30 p.m. on reports that the man from a prior welfare check call was now threatening a member of his household with a knife, according to the highway patrol. As officers talked with the reporting party in the front yard, the man exited the home, allegedly armed with a knife, and began to chase after officers. Officers retreated, but the man, still reportedly wielding a knife, continued to chase one officer, who shot the man, according to the highway patrol.

On Friday, officers responded to Chili Avenue after reports that an ex-boyfriend was trying to break into a woman’s house. According to RPD, the officers found the man on the side of the home, who immediately opened fire at the officers and the victim. The female victim and children in the home were physically uninjured. A civilian victim was shot multiple times in an exchange of gunfire with the man. Police said he is a pistol permit holder and was in legal possession of a gun during the incident. He is in serious, but not life-threatening, condition. The man ran before officers encountered him again on Thurston Road. They said the man opened fire after he was ordered to drop the weapon. The officers were injured, returned fire, and killed the man. Officers said he had an illegally possessed handgun.

Officers shot and killed a man, then found a woman who was shot and killed inside their Baytown home on Friday, police said. The incident happened around 4 a.m. Friday at an apartment complex on the 3700 block of Garth Road. Officers encountered a man who was armed with a knife outside the complex. After officers gave verbal commands, the man allegedly moved towards the officers, which led them to fire him, striking him, police said. The man was declared dead at the scene.

column7: Summit Lake Rd and Spur Dr
column12: Okanogan County Sheriff's Office, U.S. Marshals Service, Washington State Patrol
column15: An officer-involved shooting during the execution of a high-risk search warrant early Friday morning near Tonasket left one person dead, according to the Okanogan County Sheriff’s Office. The incident occurred in the early morning hours of December 19, 2025, in the area of Summit Lake Road and Spur Drive. Deputies with the Okanogan County Sheriff’s Office were assisted by the U.S. Marshals Service Special Operations Team and the Washington State Patrol SWAT Team while serving the warrant. They shot and killed the person.

Officers from the Hollywood Division were dispatched at 3:35 p.m. Thursday to an apartment complex in the 1400 block of North Bronson Avenue, near Sunset Boulevard, to reports of a possible suicide person, police said. The responding officers discovered that the man was armed with a knife, prompting officers to use a 40mm less-lethal foam launcher to subdue him, but without effect. Police said Guerrero Rojo subsequently began to charge at officers, and an “officer-involved shooting” occurred.

The agents, who were a part of the Rio Grande Valley Sector Special Operations Detachment, noticed several individuals attempting to escape back to Mexico after being approached. In the chase that ensued, one agent found himself in a dangerous altercation with one of the individuals, the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) reported. The situation escalated rapidly, leading the agent to broadcast a distress call at 4:18 p.m., stating he was, "in a fight" and needed assistance.

The Bexar County Sheriff’s Office said deputies were called to a residence around 8:30 to 8:45 a.m. after a woman reported that a man had forced his way into her home. The woman, who lives at the residence with her two children, was able to flee and call 911, officials said. When deputies attempted to make contact with the person, he retreated into a makeshift bedroom area attached to the front of the home and opened fire, officials said. The shooting occurred at close range. Investigators estimated fewer than 10 rounds were fired during the exchange. One deputy was struck in the hip and another was shot in the hand. Both sustained through-and-through wounds and returned fire, authorities said. The person was struck twice in the upper body and was pronounced dead at the scene.

Augusta County Sheriff’s Office deputies were attempting to serve an arrest warrant on a person in the 800 block of Parkersburg Turnpike. When the deputies arrived, they encountered the wanted person, and a physical altercation occurred. A deputy was shot in the upper arm area during the altercation.

The office issued an alert shortly before 5 p.m. warning residents about a hostage situation along Pittsboro Goldston Road near its intersection with U.S. Highway 421. At the time, law enforcement described a person barricaded inside a residence and one Chatham County Sheriff’s deputy being shot, injured and transported to a hospital for treatment. An update shortly after 6:30 p.m. said there was no longer an “active threat,” although it did not detail how the incident with the barricaded person and hostage was resolved. Shortly after 9 p.m., the sheriff’s office released another update sharing additional details, including deputies being called to the residence — 8247 Pittsboro Goldston Road — for an armed standoff. The situation escalated to a hostage rescue scene, according to authorities, with deputies eventually entering the residence “after developing serious concerns for the hostage’s safety.” Tuesday’s most recent update identified the deceased suspect as 50-year-old Kevin Dean Hammer, who has a different address in Goldston than the residence where the incident happened.
column32: armed standoff, aggravated assault, hostage taking, domestic disturbance

column15: Gonzales said deputies on Tuesday around 6 p.m. stopped a motorcycle in the 300 block of Virginia NE, just southwest of Wyoming and Copper, while working an Auto Theft Operation for Operation Triple Beam, a collaboration with federal authorities. She did not say why deputies pulled the motorcyclist over. “The motorcyclist fled on foot,” Gonzales said. Deputies created a perimeter with assistance from a BSCO helicopter, which tracked the person. Sometime later, deputies “reengaged the individual” near the 300 block of Wisconsin SE, near Wyoming and Zuni, Gonzales said. She said "during the encounter" at least one deputy fired at the person, killing them.

column12: Saline County Sheriff's Office, Bryant Police Department
column15: Bryant police and Saline County sheriff's office SWAT officers shot and killed a woman who opened fire on them at the end of an hourslong standoff that began late Monday with a domestic disturbance call, police said in a news release.

Just after 7:30pm, Sweetwater officers responded to reports of a shoplifting at a business on South Main Street. Officers found the person, Robinson, and chased him on foot. The TBI says Robinson then wielded a knife and "advanced toward the officers." At that point, one officer shot Robinson.

According to the Riverside County Sheriff’s Office, deputies were first called to the 16000 block of Heatherglen Road at 12:35 a.m. on reports of a residential fire. “Dispatch received multiple reports of a subject setting a fire inside the residence,” RSO said in a statement. “Deputies entered the backyard and located a subject lying on the ground,” officials said. “Deputies gave commands, but the subject failed to comply and pointed a firearm, [at which point] a deputy-involved shooting occurred.”

Officers responded around 2:44 a.m. to an alarm at Starling Chevrolet along E Irlo Bronson Memorial Highway, where St. Cloud police Chief Douglas Goerke said the man, identified by authorities on Monday as Deshay Brian Turner, was seen sitting in the passenger seat of a vehicle on the lot. According to a news release from the police department, Turner had broken into the vehicle. Turner — whom Goerke said was from the Orlando area — then ran toward the back of a nearby Wawa after being told to show his hands, the chief said. Officers briefly lost sight of Turner before finding him hiding in bushes, where police say he pulled a gun.

The TBI began its investigation at the request of 22nd Judicial District Attorney General Brent Cooper. Information released by the TBI states that preliminary information indicates a sheriff’s deputy responded to an address in the 900 block of Southport Road in Mount Pleasant Sunday, as part of an effort to locate a man at the request of Lawrence County. “Upon arrival, the deputy made contact with the man, identified as Jeremiah Dobbins,” the TBI release states. “During the encounter, Dobbins reportedly produced a weapon, resulting in the deputy firing shots, striking him. Dobbins was transported to an area hospital, where he later died.”

DPS says around 10 a.m., a sergeant was chasing a driver heading eastbound on Interstate 40. The driver reportedly went off of the freeway and headed into the desert east of Holbrook. Authorities say the person began shooting at law enforcement, who returned fire. Around 1:45 p.m., the suspect was pronounced dead at the scene. No troopers were hurt in the shooting.

column12: Oklahoma State Highway Patrol, Grady County Sheriff's Office, Tuttle Police Department
column15: According to the Oklahoma Highway Patrol, Mustang Police attempted to stop a vehicle at approximately 5 a.m., initiating the chase. OHP later joined the pursuit and took over as the primary agency. Officers from Tuttle and a Grady County deputy eventually joined the chase. According to OHP, a passenger in the vehicle fired multiple shots at OHP troopers. The pursuit ended at a home on Silver City Ridge Road in Tuttle, after the vehicle pulled over and the passenger attempted to flee on foot. The passenger broke into a home, and troopers were able to pursue and fire at the person, killing him, according to OHP

column12: South Williamsport Police Department, Pennsylvania State Police
column15: State troopers and borough police responded to the home to investigate a report that Hughes was allegedly “threatening to shoot someone with a gun,” it was stated in the release, which was issued by Trooper Lauren Lesher, the public information officer at the Troop F barracks in Montoursville. “The troopers and officers made contact with the homeowner, a member of Hughes’ family, and were invited into the residence. Upon entry, Hughes brandished a weapon at the troopers, and shots were fired,” killing Hughes, Lesher said.

column15: Deputies were called in response to a stabbing. When law enforcement found the stabbing subject, there was a brief interaction that resulted in an officer firing their weapon, striking the man.

column7: I-10 Frontage Rd and N 7th St
column15: The incident began at approximately 9:17 a.m. when Beaumont officers responded to assist Port Arthur police pursuing an armed subject, according to a Beaumont Police Department news release. The chase ended when Vital lost control of his vehicle on the I-10 service road near Seventh St, crashed, and exited the vehicle before opening fire on officers. Police shot and killed him.
column32: traffic stop, person with a weapon, pursuit

column12: Scott County Sheriff's Office, Morton Police Department
column15: Both the Scott County Sheriff’s Office and Morton Police Department were involved in the shooting. Deputies from the Scott County Sheriff’s Office responded to reports of a subject attempting to enter cars in the parking lot of a local business. When deputies arrived on the scene, the subject was seen driving a yard-truck through the lot. When deputies attempted to make contact with the subject, the subject fled and deputies began pursuit. On Highway 13, the subject collided with a cement truck, a passenger vehicle, and an occupied school bus. According to officials, deputies then “discharged their weapons in an attempt to neutralize the subject.” The subject was struck, resulting in fatal injuries.
A Border Patrol agent shot and killed a man. According to the sheriff’s office, Border Patrol agents were involved in a struggle prior to the shooting.

A man was shot and killed by a Chicago police officer investigating a stolen vehicle on the North Side Tuesday night, CPD said. Police allege the man was driving and "dragging" an officer with a vehicle when they shot him.

MSP says the sergeant and troopers went to a home to pick up a 54-year-old man on a mental health order signed by a judge. When they got there, they found him in a car. MSP said he pulled a weapon and “shots were fired” — though police did not immediately list the exact series of events regarding who fired shots and in what order.

column12: Mooreland Police Department, Woodward County Sheriff's Office
column15: Deputies responded to reports of a reckless driver. They allege the man "produced a firearm" and they sht and killed him.

According to Greenville County Sheriff's Lt. Ryan Flood, authorities received a 911 call just before 11:30 p.m. on Dec. 9 reporting that a woman at 2627 Poinsett Highway had been assault. Deputies responding to the address in the Poinsett View Apartments encountered a man with a weapon, according to Flood. One deputy fired on the man, identified as Johndy Lading Rodriguez, 29. He was pronounced dead at the scene.
Police shot and killed a man in response to an assault with a deadly weapon call. They allege he was armed with a gun.

column7: N 7th Ave and W Yukon Dr
column15: A man is dead after being shot by police in north Phoenix on Sunday afternoon. According to the Phoenix Police Department, the shooting happened just before noon near 7th Avenue and Beardsley Road, just north of Loop 101. Police responded to the area for reports of a man with a gun. As they searched the neighborhood, one of the officers at the scene found the person. Sergeant Robert Scherer with Phoenix Police said it was then that the officer told the suspect to drop his weapon. Scherer said that the perrson did not comply and instead walked toward the officer and pointed the gun at him. Police shot and killed him.

Officials said the incident began when officers responded to reports of a vehicle stopped in the roadway with no lights on at North First Street shortly after 6 p.m. The caller reported the driver staring straight ahead and not responding to knocks on his window, the DA's office said. When officers tried to talk to the driver, the man drove away and entered eastbound Interstate 80. The driver exited the freeway at Pedrick Road and eventually pulled over on Sievers Road near the Chevron station. The DA's office said the driver displayed a black handgun while seated in the vehicle, which later turned out to be a BB gun. After refusing officers' commands, the driver got out of the car while holding the gun in his right hand and then raised it in the direction of officers, the DA's office said. Police shot and killed him.

Two officers were on patrol around 9:30 p.m. in the 800 block of South Philadelphia Street when they stopped to talk with some people in front of a home, Sgt. Matt Sutter said. Police shot and killed Alberto but have not disclosed details about what happened.

column7: Tremont Blvd NW and Mt Mercy Dr NW
column15: On Monday, GRPD released dashboard and body-worn camera video of the traffic stop and shooting Saturday afternoon on Tremont Boulevard NW west of Mt. Mercy Drive. Police had pulled over the driver after two separate calls from the family home that he was intoxicated and making threats with a gun. “Shut off the car, shut off the car, shut off the car. Turn the key. Turn the car off,” officers can be heard commanding in the video. Twenty-seven seconds after the traffic stop, Martinez opened his car door while opening fire, pulling the trigger up to a dozen times, police said. Police shot and killed him.

Senior Trooper William Miller was dispatched to the crash scene. First responders on scene reported that an involved party was armed with a gun before Miller arrived. When Miller encountered the armed person, they continued to show a gun and was not complying with commands, troopers said. Troopers said Miller shot the man.
column32: person with a gun, car crash

column15: The AG's office said the situation started around 4:43 p.m. Saturday when police responded to the area of South Mammoth Road in Manchester for a report of a suspicious vehicle. Inside, police found a man - later identified as Turenne - asleep at the wheel and a woman asleep in the passenger seat. When the man woke up, police say he sped off. Police said they were met at the door to the home by an unclothed woman holding a butcher-style kitchen knife. Police said she charged at officers holding the knife, prompting an officer to fire.

Police say they were called to a business in the 2900 block of Parkway Drive at 3:22 a.m. on July 5th for a report of a fight in progress involving up to 100 people. Police say at 3:34 a.m., while officers were on scene, the person, 17-year-old Terrence Hastings Jr., began shooting at other people outside the business. An LPD officer saw the person as he was shooting and immediately began chasing him as the suspect ran away. “While running after him, the officer gave verbal commands for the person to show his hands. Instead, the person again leveled his weapon in the direction of individuals on scene, prompting the officer to fire his department-issued weapon. Even after being shot, the person continued to crawl toward and reach for his weapon, prompting the officer to again fire his weapon at the suspect. Hastings was pronounced deceased at the scene,” police said.

According to the Sheriff’s Information Bureau, deputies were dispatched about 4:30 a.m. Friday to a “shots fired” call in the 1500 block of Helen Drive, just southwest of the San Bernardino (10) and Long Beach (710) freeway interchange. Upon arriving, deputies located the man and contacted him, when he “produced a handgun and fired at deputies, at which point a deputy-involved shooting occurred,” according to the SIB.

According to police, around 6 p.m. Friday, the man reportedly began shooting at officers on the 2900 block of Lawrence Street while police were responding to a domestic incident. When officers approached the door to the home, a 40-year-old man inside grabbed a gun and began firing at police. The man left the home and kept shooting, and police returned fire. The man allegedly attempted to steal a police car, all while he was still shooting at police, with officers returning fire, and continuing after the man got out of the car and was on the ground.
column33: Mary Gasperone, Melvin Douglas Griffin III

column15: A driver called 911 from 12th Street around 7:40 a.m., saying a man was pointing a gun at traffic and had aimed it at her, Police Chief Shawn Caldwell said. When the first officer got to the scene, the man shot at her several times as she was getting out of her vehicle, Caldwell said. The officer returned fire, and the man ran off. The man shot at a second officer as they arrived and continued running into a neighborhood, Caldwell said. He hid somewhere in the neighborhood, and officers surrounded the area. A neighbor told police they believed the suspect was in a shed, Caldwell said. He then came out of hiding and ran toward SWAT officers, firing at them. They shot and killed him.

Ninth Precinct officers on routine patrol in the area noticed three masked people standing beside a building, the chief told reporters. In a neighborhood that has reported a recent uptick in breaking-and-entering incidents, the officers found the trio suspicious and stopped to investigate, Bettison said. They detained one person while the other two led them on a foot pursuit, according to the chief. When the officers apprehended another person, Bettison said, “a brief struggle occurred. The person was reaching for a handgun, trying to get it, was able to get the handgun and shot one of our officers in … what I'm being told (was) the left hand. At that point, (police) returned fire, fatally wounding the individual.”

Deputies responded to a family disturbance involving an armed individual at a home in the 400 block of Bonham Street at about 11:10 p.m. Upon arrival, GCSO said deputies encountered Nathan Edwards, 32, who was allegedly armed. They shot and killed him.
column32: domestic disturbance, person with a weapon

column7: Town Creek Dr and Glen Oaks Blvd
column15: Cedar Hill Police officers initiated a vehicle pursuit in the 700 block of Highway 67 involving a driver believed to be impaired. The person fled from officers, leading them on a pursuit that continued into the City of Dallas. Cedar Hill police say at approximately 2:16 p.m., the person exited the vehicle and fled on foot into a wooded area. During the foot pursuit, one Cedar Hill officer discharged his firearm, striking the person.

column7: N Bartlett Ave and E Kenmore Pl
column15: Early this morning, one person was killed and two others were shot in Shorewood, including a Shorewood police officer. While searching for the person, a chase began that ended at Finlayson Street and West Reservoir Avenue. At this scene an additional person was pronounced deceased. Police shot and killed the person after an extended shootout and standoff.

column12: San Luis Obispo County Sheriff's Office
column15: Officers responded to a call in the 2300 block of Fresno Street regarding suspicious circumstances. A woman expressed concern for her safety because of a man living in the nearby area. Sheriff's officials say the 40-year-old Chowchilla resident was described as having a history of violent behavior, as well as possessing weapons. Additional deputies arrived on the scene just after midnight. When they made contact with the male subject, sheriff's officials say he pulled out a handgun. In response, deputies fired and the man was struck. It was a pellet gun.
A parole officer stopped a man in a vehicle while conducting an investigation. The person tried to drive away with the parole officer's hand in the window and the officer shot and killed them.
column16: Charged with murder, aggravated assault, simple assault and reckless endangerment

column15: According to Selman, deputies were trying to arrest John Franklin Carter, 50, when he was shot. Deputies were patrolling Stubblefield Road off of U.S. 69 north of Lufkin at 7:59 a.m. and looking for Carter and saw a white 2018 Toyota leaving a home. Recognizing it as Carter’s vehicle, deputies approached it when a woman driver suddenly left the car. Selman said Carter began acting upset and got out of the vehicle and was holding the gun and said he “was not going back to prison.” Deputies told Carter multiple times to drop the gun but Carter refused, Selman said. A deputy fired his gun and struck Carter.

A Thousand Oaks man died Tuesday evening after being shot by a Ventura County Sheriff’s deputy. The deputy had been responding to an 8 p.m. call reporting the man was armed and experiencing a mental health issue, the sheriff’s office said. When deputies arrived at the home in the 500 block of Racquet Club Lane, a member of the family came outside to speak with them, said VCSO Sgt. Monica Smith. She did not know how many, if any, other family members were inside the home. During the course of the conversation between the family member and deputies, the 23-year-old man, whose identity has not yet been made public, came onto the home’s balcony and discharged a round, the sheriff’s office said in a statement issued Wednesday morning. That’s when the deputy fired, VCSO said.

column12: Dubuque County Sheriff's Office, Dubuque Police Department, Monticello Police Department
column15: One man is dead and a Dubuque County Sheriff's Deputy is hurt following a shooting during what county officials called a "high-risk traffic stop" early Tuesday morning. It happened just before 4:30 a.m. after deputies stopped a vehicle on Highway 151 just north of the Highway 136 interchange near Cascade. Dubuque County Sheriff Joe Kennedy said in a press release the unnamed adult male produced a gun and that shots were fired.
column33: Adam Williams, Chad Leitzen, Cole Millard

column15: Troopers were called to O’Neil Road in the town of Norfolk at around 12:45 a.m. for a report of a domestic dispute involving a knife. Footage shows Russo coming out of an RV on the property. He appears to be holding an object, which police tell him to drop. He complies. A trooper orders him to get on the ground. Again, he complies. The video shows Russo ranting and writhing on the grass. A trooper is seen putting on gloves before approaching Russo, who struggles as police place him in handcuffs and leg restraints. He died soon thereafter.

Deputies responded to Old Timers Court in the Lamar area of Darlington County around 1:30 a.m. in reference to a wanted person, according to August. During the response, August said two deputies were ambushed. One of the deputies, Devin Mason, 27, died. August said the other deputy was taken to the hospital for treatment where he is stable. Sheriff August said the man, 25-year-old Cameron Ray Dennett, was killed. Dennett was prohibited from having a firearm and had active warrants for criminal conspiracy, forgery and second degree computer act.

column12: Zillah Police Department, Granger Police Department
column15: Zillah police were called to the 200 block of First Avenue around 12:10 a.m. July 1 for a man who was inside his neighbor’s home, according to an earlier YVSIU release. Zillah and Granger officers responded to the scene, and Leal refused to leave the house as officers negotiated with him for more than an hour, the first release said. Police eventually went in to remove Leal, and there “was a confrontation, and a use of force occurred that did not involve a firearm.”

A police statement said that the young man, who was not identified, was "threatening to kill everyone in the home." When police responded to a 911 call, the department said the man "rushed officers with a knife." An unknown number of officers fired.

The woman, who has not been identified, called 911, threatening to kill herself and hurt anyone who came into the house. Deputies and medics went to a home in the 200 block of Mountain Laurel Drive, where the call was made from. For about 30 minutes, deputies said they tried to speak with the woman while 911 operators called her phone. The woman spoke briefly with the dispatcher and hung up several times, the sheriff’s office said. Then the woman opened the front door and pointed a handgun at deputies, according to the sheriff’s office. Deputies shot her, and she collapsed inside the home.

According to the sheriff's office, a deputy had encountered a car in the area just over a mile south of Niles, Mich. When the deputy approached, however, a man got out and ran off while the driver sped away on Third Street, deputies said. As the deputy chased after the passenger, the man pulled out a gun and fired it at the deputy. The deputy then returned fire, killing the man, according to the sheriff's office.

Officers were called to Betty G. Ross Park on Madison Street, around 1:25 p.m. in response to a ‘domestic incident’. When officers arrived, they found a woman who had been shot multiple times. Officers said this led to an officer-involved shooting that left a man dead at the scene. Police did not give details on what led up to the fatal shooting.

Elk Grove police officers responded to a call for service at the Chevron (10610 Promenade Parkway) regarding a man attempting to gain access to the employee office, going behind the cash register area, and who possibly appeared to be under the influence of narcotics on June 28, 2025, around 12:16 p.m. Officers arrived on scene and contacted the 37-year-old man. When officers attempted to detain the man, he immediately began to physically resist the officers. Additional officers arrived and assisted with detaining the man; eventually placing him in handcuffs after a four-to-five-minute struggle. Police then used a WRAP device against the person. He died soon thereafter.

column7: W Orchard St and S 91st St
column15: Police were called for a reported shooting near 91st and Orchard. When officers arrived at the scene, they found an armed 72-year-old. Officers ordered that person to drop the weapon, Mitchell said, but the person refused. Officers then shot that person, who died at the scene.

US Marshals attempted to apprehend a man on warrants for aggravated assault, aggravated assault, domestic violence, disorderly conduct with a weapon, misconduct involving weapons, threats and assault. They found the man at a residence, and they continued their surveillance as he drove away from the home. "Task Force members attempted to stop the vehicle when the fugitive fired multiple rounds at law enforcement. The subject was struck by police gunfire and succumbed to his wounds," said a spokesperson for the US Marshals Service.

column12: California Highway Patrol, Del Norte County Sheriff's Office
column15: California Highway Patrol (CHP) officers assigned to the CHP Crescent City Area responded to a 911 report of a male subject covered in blood, on Anchor Way west of US-101. Emergency medical personnel also responded to the scene. The male subject was carrying a knife and aggressively approached medical personnel. Medical personnel backed away from the male subject. One Del Norte Sheriff’s Office (DNSO) deputy and two CHP officers arrived on the scene and ordered the subject to drop the knife. The male subject was non-responsive to verbal commands. The subject aggressively approached the deputy and officers. The DNSO deputy deployed his electronic control device, which proved to be ineffective. The subject continued to aggressively charge at the officers with a knife, and out of fear for his safety and the safety of others, a CHP officer involved shooting occurred.

Phillips County Sheriff’s Office received a report of illegal fireworks being detonated at 899 1st Street in Phillipsburg. A Phillips County deputy, initially identified as the Undersheriff by other agencies but later clarified by the Sedgwick County Sheriff’s office as not serving in that capacity at the time of his death, responded to the scene. Upon arrival, the deputy made contact with Kolton Griffith, who was believed to be responsible for the fireworks. During the encounter, the deputy developed probable cause to arrest Griffith. As the deputy attempted to place Griffith in handcuffs, a struggle ensued. Griffith reportedly pulled a concealed handgun and opened fire on the deputy. Despite being struck by gunfire, Deputy Gaede returned fire, hitting Griffith multiple times. Griffith died at the scene.

Police say it began at around 5:30 p.m. at the Mercantile Bank in Saginaw Township on State Street between Mitchell Street and Berberovich Drive. The situation involved a barricaded subject keeping a hostage at the bank. Michigan State Police Lt. Kim Vetter says a trooper engaged and fatally shot the man when they presented themselves.
Police responded to a disturbance involving weapons. They attempted to arrest a man who they allege fought them and shot and officer before being shot and killed by police.

According to Multnomah County District Attorney Nathan Vasquez, the still-unreleased medical examiner's report describes the cause and manner of death as "prone restraint cardiac arrest with a contributing cause of acute methamphetamine intoxication." Officers J.P. Duque Valencia, Travis Wortman and Jason Epton, who restrained Johnson prior to his death the night of June 27, had been responding to reports that he was having a mental health crisis.

Police said that around 11:56 p.m. on Thursday, June 26, they tried to stop a motorcycle on U.S. Highway 70 for allegedly failing to display a registration plate, speeding and reckless driving. According to police, the driver – later identified as Camden Skyler Childers of Stanley – did not stop and drove off at a high rate of speed into Conover. After a pursuit, the man crashed and allegedly fought with an officer before being shot and killed by police.

A stolen vehicle was tracked to the 3800 block of Casa Colorado Avenue in Las Vegas, Nevada. Detectives obtained probable cause and secured a search warrant for a residence associated with the suspect. The stolen vehicle was recovered a short distance away. At approximately 7:00 a.m. on June 26, 2025, the Henderson Police Department’s SWAT team served the warrant at the residence. Upon entry, officers encountered a 71-year-old male armed with a firearm. During the encounter, one officer discharged his weapon, striking the male.
Melton died in the early morning of June 25 after being restrained by police officers during a mental health crisis the night before.

column15: Police received a call around 2 p.m. Wednesday about a woman who may have been experiencing a behavioral health crisis on Wednesday afternoon, according to Baltimore Police Commissioner Richard Worley. Police shot and killed her after they allege she lunged at them with a knife.

Nevada State Police say sheriff's deputies initially responded to a domestic disturbance call near Pickering Avenue around 7:30 p.m. when the shooting happened. NSP hasn't released many specifics other than an unidentified man died and no officers were hurt in the incident.

Virginia State Police say about 7:00 a.m. June 25, 2025, county deputies responded to a 911 call from a man, Liam Gerald McCaul, 23 of Nashville, who said he had killed his father, Hugh Gerard McCaul, 58 of Troutville. Deputies saw the younger man, armed, outside the home on High Ridge Circle. While working to get him to surrender, the sheriff’s office said, the man pointed a gun at deputies, leading deputies to shoot and kill him.

The Brooklyn Police Department responded to a request for assistance from the Parma Heights Police just before 11 a.m. They were in pursuit of a Black F-150 pickup truck with Parma Police, and it crashed at Tiedeman Road and I-480 with two other vehicles. Numerous attempts by Brooklyn’s crisis negotiator to get the driver of the pick-up truck to surrender peacefully were unsuccessful, and SWAT was called to take over the scene. Due to the threat from the pick-up truck driver, Tiedeman Road was closed in both directions. According to police, after 4-plus hours of negotiations, the man was shot by a tactical officer when he exited his vehicle with a gun in his hand.

Bonath said the shooting, which is being investigated by the Lubbock Metropolitan Special Crimes Unit, stemmed from an encounter at about 12:45 a.m. after two officers, who were working an unrelated traffic violation in the 2700 block of the Marsha Sharp Freeway access road, noticed a suspicious activity in the parking lot on the north side of the Jones AT&T Stadium. Bonath declined to comment further, citing the ongoing investigation, but a Texas Tech police news release stated that during the encounter, the person drew a weapon and shot at the officers, who returned fire.

Sgt. Mark Trippe said a Homewood officer was investigating a suspicious vehicle at the park. The park was otherwise empty at the time, police said. Peoples, police said, was inside the vehicle engaged in a physical altercation and then pulled a gun. The officer then shot Peoples.

Officers responded to a shots-fired call at 5:14 p.m. at a home in the 600 block of Timber Hill Drive. Police said that when officers arrived, they located a man on the porch with a weapon in hand. Officers said the man refused commands to drop his weapon and police shot and killed him.

column12: Denver Police Department, Denver Public Schools Police
column15: Denver police officers and a DPS safety officer responded to a report of a man and woman standing in front of Kepner Beacon Middle School, near S. Federal Boulevard and W. Kentucky Ave. While Denver police were looking into if the man or woman had any outstanding warrants for their arrests, the man asked if he could leave. Officers said no, and that's when DPD said he ran off. As officers chased after him, they instructed the man to drop the weapon. He did not and shot a gun at officers, Chief Thomas said. When the two DPD offices and DPS safety officer shot back, they hit the man.
column33: Mitch Nordskog, Whitney Rohrback, Kyle Lucero.

column15: Colorado Springs Police Department (CSPD) received a call regarding shots fired at an apartment located in the 1400 block of Michelle Court, near Fountain Boulevard and Murray Boulevard. Officers began investigating and encountered a man who was holding a firearm. According to CSPD Officer Daniel Short, officers gave commands to the man, and at that time, the suspect raised his firearm and shot at least once towards officers. Two officers then fired at least one shot at the man.

FDLE is investigating after two Orange County deputies shot and killed a 57-year-old man who they say wouldn’t drop a knife. It happened at the Isles at East Millenia Apartments on Lake Fountain Drive. The man’s girlfriend told deputies he held her against her will with a knife throughout Sunday night until she escaped Monday around noon. She called 911 from the apartment complex’s leasing office. She told deputies her boyfriend had been smoking drugs throughout the night. “From her standpoint, she could not get out. So, she did not feel comfortable trying to leave,” said Undersheriff Mark Canty. Deputies found the man barricaded in the apartment. SWAT tried to negotiate for hours until deputies say he walked out with a knife “He started moving toward the deputies. He refused to comply with their instructions, and they felt like they needed to fire their weapons,” Canty said. Both deputies who shot at the man are now on administrative leave per protocol as FDLE investigates.

Officers say it started when they responded to a wounding call at a Shell gas station on 4260 Winchester Road around 5:50 a.m. A man was found suffering from a stab wound at the scene. Police say they also found a man armed with a screwdriver who had allegedly stabbed the wounded victim. Police allege the man tried to stab them and they shot and killed him.

The Utah County Sheriff's Office said they learned of an "aggravated" sexual assault incident that occurred between Sunday night and Monday morning in Eagle Mountain. Police obtained a search warrant and sent a SWAT team to the man's home around noon "due to the level of violence displayed by the man." When SWAT entered the home, the man was armed with a handgun. Officials said the officers ordered him to drop the gun and surrender, but he refused and instead pointed the gun at them. That's when the SWAT team used "lethal force," according to a press release from the sheriff's office.

column7: 112th St S and C St S
column15: Deputies responded at 4:21 p.m. to a report of a man who was allegedly involved in previous burglaries breaking and throwing objects, and then trying to light a building on fire, sheriff’s office spokesperson Carly Cappetto said. Deputies confronted him at the Pacific Pride gas station in the 110th block of Pacific Avenue South and pursued him on foot for a few blocks to the area of 112th Street South and C Street South, where deputies said shots were fired, Cappetto said.

Authorities first responded to the scene around 6 a.m. after receiving reports of a man in a boat who was possibly shooting a firearm at people on another boat, HPD Chief Joe Logan said at a press conference. However, at around 12:50 p.m., the man allegedly pointed a shotgun-style firearm at officers around 15 to 20 feet away, Logan said. That’s when authorities say a Specialized Services Division officer discharged a single round, striking the man in the cheek.

Lenexa Police say they were called to an apartment complex in the 12400 block of West 97th Terrace for a report of a person with a gun at about 3 a.m. According to the department’s calls for service log, the first-responder drone was also used. “During the encounter with that individual, at least one Lenexa officer discharged their firearm, striking the individual,” Chavez said in the release.

column7: S Sarah St and Manchester Ave
column15: A secondary officer spotted the person allegedly involved in an earlier shooting near Manchester and Sarah and tried to pull him over but the man took off. The chase ended in a vacant lot on Clayton and Vandeventer. Police say the man got off the moped, refused orders, and allegedly reached into a bag. That’s when two detectives fired, killing him.

Police say they responded to a report of a possible fight in a vehicle and tried to make contact, but the vehicle led them on a brief chase that ended in the 7800 Block of Broad River Road. Police said Jackson, the driver and only occupant, got into an altercation with officers. Jackson was allegedly "dry tased" and restrained by police. He died soon thereafter.

An off-duty San Bernardino County sheriff's deputy shot and killed a homicide suspect Saturday night after two victims were fatally shot in the parking lot of a Fontana shopping center, authorities said.

A man who had locked himself inside a restroom at a McDonald’s in Riverside and who police say later fought with officers died at a hospital after they used force on him, the Riverside Police Department said. The confrontation happened around 6:30 a.m. on Friday, June 20, at the restaurant at 7474 Indiana St., near Madison Street and the 91 Freeway, a department news release said. An employee told police the man did not respond when they asked him to leave the restroom. Officers, however, were able to get him out. “The man became combative and force was used to detain him,” the release said. “Medical aid responded, and while being treated by paramedics, he remained combative before going into medical distress. He was transported to a local hospital, where medical staff provided treatment for over an hour. Despite their efforts, the man later died.” Police declined to describe the force used.

CCSO deputies said it happened June 20 around 3:45 p.m. at the 5700 block of Indian Trail in Keystone Heights. They were at the residence to serve multiple arrest warrants on Dajshon Travis Asbell. Deputies and K9s spent several hours attempting to negotiate with Asbell for a peaceful surrender, all of which they said Asbell ignored. After using tear gas, deputies allege Asbell exited with a sharp edged weapon and they shot him.
Investigators have released new details and say officers were responding to a well-being check when they opened fire and fatally shot a 59-year-old man armed with a knife in Highland Park.

Louisiana State Police say their initial investigation shows the incident stemmed from a domestic violence complaint involving an armed subject on St. John Street. A family member tells KNOE the man was suffering from a mental health crisis, and domestic violence was not involved. Officials say when they arrived on scene the subject had barricaded himself inside a room. They say deputies attempted to negotiate with the subject, and when he came out of the room he was armed. They shot and killed him.

Sheriff's Office deputies apprehended Lovett at the Quick N’ Fast convenience store located at 6008 White Horse Road, following a call about an armed robbery there, according to Flood. Deputies said a man had entered the store and demanded money, armed with a knife. A member of the Sheriff's Office K-9 Unit bit Lovett as deputies arrested him. He died soon thereafter.

A use of force investigation was underway Friday into the fatal police shooting of a 27-year-old man who allegedly drew a knife and moved against officers who responded to an East Hollywood burglary report.

According to an ECSO news release, deputies received a call just before 3 p.m. on June 19 after a person saw a 37-year-old man who was wanted for multiple felonies. Deputies arrived at the location where he was seen, the Arby’s on Highway 98, where they also saw the man. Once the man saw deputies he allegedly ran from a car into the store with the deputies following right behind him. Officials said the man then jumped over the counter and fought with one of the three deputies before pushing the deputy to the ground. “The man then turned and moved aggressively towards the deputies with the knife,” according to the release. “The three deputies fired at the man, striking him several times. The man died on the scene.”

According to Madison Polston, Public Affairs Director for Brazoria Co. Sheriff’s Office , it all started when a woman called 911 about an “impending disturbance.” She said an unidentified man may have been on his way to her home, and deputies knew he had outstanding warrants for assault charges. At the scene, Polston was unable to disclose what the relationship was between the two, but the man wasn’t at the location that responding officers arrived at. However, investigators did notice a car matching the man’s vehicle’s description “committing a traffic violation.” That same car then turned into the victim’s neighborhood, and when deputies tried to pull the driver over, he fled, and a chase ensued. Deputies set up a perimeter while the driver sped off, going the opposite direction on the highway before crashing into a ditch. He then got out of his car and took off on foot into a wooded area. Deputies were able to find him in the densely wooded area, where they said he brandished a knife when they tried to arrest him. Two deputies then fired at him.

The mother of Benedetti reported her vehicle stolen after he had taken the vehicle to get an illegal narcotic that helps people who are withdrawing from drug abuse.Deputies found the vehicle and performed a traffic stop, where they came across Benedetti and a passenger in the vehicle. IRCSO said Benedetti was somewhat following deputies' orders until he began to reach into his pockets and waistbands as if he were searching for a weapon. Deputies gave numerous commands telling the man to show his hands. Benedetti disobeyed those commands and even tried to charge one of the deputies, which led to the deputy-involved shooting.
According to Kentucky State Police, Hayley Davidson was shot by Bearl Ashcraft Jr., a special deputy who was serving in the Lee County Sheriff's Office, before he took his own life.

According to the Chautauqua County Sheriff’s Office, around 3:30 p.m. Wednesday the department received a call of a domestic incident at 2900 Mina French Creek Road. Initial response had two deputies who were both on scene by 3:55 p.m. Upon arrival at the residence deputies encountered an armed subject who was outside the residence with a shotgun who allegedly fired off one round from the gun at that point. They shot and killed him.

Around 5:15 p.m., MDSO deputies with the Robbery Intervention Detail tried to pull over 24-year-old Kristofer Lazaro Laboy, in the area of 66th Street and Northwest 22nd Avenue for having dark tints on his car, the sheriff’s office said. He sped away, refusing to stop, then a chase began, per deputies. A helicopter overhead helped deputies track down the yellow Corvette to a dead-end in an apartment community in the area of Northwest Fourth Court and Northwest 85th Street, just a mile away from where the pursuit began. After Laboy hopped out of the Corvette armed, deputies say Deputy Kelvin Cox, a 23-year veteran, opened fire, striking him.

Officers were patrolling near the intersection of Pennsylvania Avenue and Laurens Street when they observed an adult male believed to be armed. During the encounter, the male pointed a handgun and fired at an officer. One officer was struck in the foot, and three officers returned fire, striking the male.
column33: Devin Yancy, Omar Rodriguez, Ashley Negron

column15: According to a Missouri State Highway Patrol spokesperson, around 6:17 p.m. Tuesday, troopers were notified by the Concordia, Missouri, Police Department that one of their officers had initiated a pursuit of a motorcycle being operated by a man wanted in an out-of-state homicide. While officers lost sight of the motorcycle, about 90 minutes later, troopers in the area spotted the motorcycle. Troopers say the man crashed the motorcycle into a trooper’s patrol car and then fled on foot. During the chase, troopers say Alcantar-Chavez, armed with a handgun, opened fire and struck a trooper in his bulletproof vest. The trooper returned fire, fatally striking Alcantar-Chavez.

According to NMSP, Gallagher was wanted on an outstanding probation violation warrant. The United States Marshals Service went to a residence frequented by Gallagher on Echols Avenue on Monday. Upon approaching the home, Gallagher fled on foot. A pursuit through a nearby alleyway began. Marshals deployed their tasers in an attempt to stop Gallagher. According to NMPS, Gallagher brandished a firearm. Two members of USMS shot Gallagher.

A woman was shot and killed Tuesday morning in an officer-involved shooting with the Albuquerque Police Department. Tuesday evening, APD identified the woman as Desiree Herrera. APD said the shooting happened at the Hotel Parq Central. APD Police Chief Harold Medina said around 4:30 a.m., a call came in from the hotel about a woman in a mental health crisis that they would like to be removed and trespassed from the hotel. Medina said Herrera was able to disarm the security guard and take the guard’s gun. When officers arrived on scene, they observed that shots had already been fired into an SUV in the parking lot, and Herrera was waving the firearm and discharged it. Medina said officers gave Herrera commands to drop the firearm. At one point, a round was fired in the direction of officers and struck an SUV in front of them. Officers returned fire, and Herrera was killed on scene.

column15: On June 16, 2025, Gary Leon Eagle Jr., died after a violent encounter with police in Red Bluff, California. He was stopped, thrown to the ground, and his untreated hernia ruptured.

Fire crews and deputies with the Churchill County Sheriff’s Office were called to Trento Lane for reports of a fire at an encampment near Mustang Pond. The LCSO says that at some point, there was an altercation and deputies shot and killed a person living at the camp.

Officials say officers responded to a home in the 3500 block of SW 17th St. around 5:30 p.m. on Monday, June 16. Upon arrival, the man, 41-year-old Eddie Hill, opened the door armed with a knife. According to police, Hill charged at officers with the knife. He was ordered to drop the weapon, but he continued to charge at officers, leading to Hill being shot by police.
