When a deputy arrived at a home in the 28000 block of Hyde Avenue, the man allegedly brandished a rifle, the Owyhee Sheriff’s Office said. He refused “numerous commands” to drop the firearm, and “shots were fired,” the release said.
Police shot and killed a young Black man. Few additional details are available.

Around 3 a.m. at a gas station in the 2400 block of New Lewisburg Highway in Columbia, deputies were called to a report of possible drug activity and a couple fighting. When officers arrived, they found a man and a woman in a car on the side of the building. After a short time, the TBI said the man, identified as 25-year-old Clayton Tyler Dodson, pulled out a firearm and shot the deputy in the vest. Both deputies returned fire and struck Dodson.

According to the Texas Department of Public Safety, Weatherford police responded to a 911 call at the business. The business owner told police that the business was being burglarized and the owner stopped the burglary, a DPS spokesperson said in a news release. The person who shot the alleged burglar was an off-duty Arlington police officer.

column7: E Trent Ave and N Pines Rd
column12: Spokane County Sheriff's Office, Washington State Patrol
column15: The Spokane County Sheriff's Office says the man carjacked mulitple vehicles and shot and killed someone before being seen driving westbound on East Trent Avenue. The man reportedly shot at law enforcement with an AR-style rifle. SCSO says Washington State Patrol troopers were on the scene of a different crash at East Trent Avenue and North Pines Road when the man crashed into a car and a trooper's car at the intersection. The sheriff's office says the man got out of the car and fired at WSP troopers. They shot and killed him.

According to AST, around 11:30 p.m. Saturday evening, multiple troopers were searching a property in Houston along Gaunt Lane for 34-year-old Kyle Lambert, a resident of Wasilla. Troopers state that he had an active felony warrant for his arrest. Lambert was hiding in a camper on the property and refused to come out, according to troopers. “As troopers entered the camper to arrest the man, he produced a handgun. Due to his actions, the man was shot by multiple troopers,” the report stated.
column33: Jacob Barker, Kody Haley, Edward Owens

column15: Police shot and killed a man they allege pointed a gun at them after responding to a family disturbance.

According to Weis, deputies responded to a call from a a family regarding the man who was having a mental health crisis. Deputies said when they arrived, the man emerged from a patch of woods naked and armed with a gun. “The subject charged our deputies and both of our deputes had to fire their firearms and then stop the subject," Weis said.

According to Miami Police, they responded to reports of a commotion around 3 a.m. as the bars were closing. “Officers observed a male, who was armed. Subsequently, several officers discharged their firearms,” said Miami Police Officer Michael Vega. Authorities said Lindo had a gun, but have not confirmed who was the first to fire. Also in the area was 28-year-old Evelyn Valdes who was driving in the area after celebrating her birthday when she was caught in the crossfire of the gunshots.

Police reported a man in distress died while being restrained by police and fire personnel who were responding to a call about a medical emergency at an apartment building near downtown Caldwell. They calim they restrained him using “minor physical force and body weight,” and placed handcuffs on him, “in an attempt to save the man from harming himself or others.”

Officers responded to Summervillage Mobile Home Park on Winter Drive after receiving a 911 call asking them to perform a welfare check in connection to a domestic dispute, according to the State Law Enforcement Division. When police arrived, they heard a gunshot from inside the residence. A Summerville officer entered and encountered a man armed with a handgun. The officer fired, shooting the person identified as Patrick David Hatcher, according to the Dorchester County Coroner’s Office.

Primitivo had a warrant for his arrest for failure to pay child support. He resisted deputies who attempted to arrest him at about 9:40 p.m. on June 13, according to a PCSO report. As he fought deputies, his brother, Francisco, approached and struck a deputy in the head with a 3.5-foot-long, 2-by-4 piece of lumber, injuring him, officials said. Francisco was then preparing to hit the deputies again when he was shot by the deputies, according to Sheriff Grady Judd.

column12: Gresham Police Department, Multnomah County Sheriff's Office
column15: Gresham police and Multnomah County sheriff’s deputies responded to a call about a physical disturbance involving an armed person at about 7:30 p.m. on Northeast 162nd Avenue near Glisan Street. They chased him, shot a less lethal round at him and then shot and killed him.

That shooting happened at the intersection of Park Avenue and Grand Street. The TBI said Memphis officers approached a large group of people in the parking lot of a business. As an officer exited his squad car, state authorities said Cook drove his vehicle "aggressively toward the officer" and hit him. Police shot and killed him.

A man was shot and killed by Beaumont Police officers after he shot and wounded an officer. It happened during the noon hour on Thursday as police were blocking traffic at a house fire in north Beaumont. Police said after he shot the officer, he then tried to get inside a patrol unit to get another weapon inside of it.

column12: Arkansas State Police, U.S. Marshals Service
column15: Millan-Gomez was wanted in connection with an armed carjacking and kidnapping that took place on Monday, June 9, 2025, in Manistee County, Michigan. During that incident, Millan-Gomez allegedly threatened a woman with a handgun, forced her to drive, and later took control of her vehicle. Law enforcement considered Millan-Gomez armed and dangerous. ASP Troopers and officers with the U.S. Marshals Service stopped Millan-Gomez on Interstate 40 East, near the 180-mile marker about a mile west of Carlisle, at about 1:30 p.m. Millan-Gomez exited his vehicle and brandished a weapon. Troopers shot and killed him.

column7: E Guadalupe Rd and Lindsay Rd
column15: On June 11, 2025, at approximately 6:00 PM, Gilbert Police Officers were dispatched to a welfare check call for service near Lindsay and Guadalupe Roads in Gilbert. It was reported that a male motorist was slumped over behind the wheel of a vehicle in the eastbound lanes of Guadalupe Road. When officers arrived, they encountered a single male, identified as 24-year-old Jacob Allen Rose, slumped over in the driver’s seat, and attempted to contact him. The officers knocked on the window, waking Rose, who acknowledged the officers. The officers asked Rose to exit the vehicle when, moments later, at about 6:04 PM, Rose reached for and armed himself with a firearm and pointed it in the direction of our officers, posing an immediate and deadly threat to our officers. Officers responded to the threat by firing their duty weapons.

The standoff began around 6 p.m. when deputies arrived at a home on Turan Road in Saucier to pick Simmons up for a mental evaluation. David Simmons, his brother, said the family obtained a court order on Wednesday because Jason Simmons struggled with substance abuse and mental health. A four-hour standoff between a Harrison County Sheriff’s Office SWAT team and a man who barricaded himself in a shed ended Wednesday night when the man was shot and killed in an exchange of gunfire with law enforcement, authorities said.

Pasco County Colonel Tait Sanborn said deputies first tried to make contact with Cristian Javier Estrada Perez on June 4 to serve him a court order for a mental health evaluation on behalf of his family. The family reportedly told deputies that Perez exhibited “erratic behavior" and had made threats to them. They told authorities he was also known to carry a gun. After an unsuccessful attempt to contact Perez on June 4, deputies attempted to serve the order again on June 5, 6 and 9. According to Sanborn, deputies returned on June 10 with a plan to talk to Perez. Deputies said Perez did not respond to multiple attempts to communicate with him. After a warning and several requests for Perez to exit the home, deputies deployed pepper balls inside. That's when, according to the sheriff's office, Perez fired four rounds at deputies from a gun that was strapped to his hand. Two deputies returned fire, Colonel Sanborn said. Perez was shot and killed.

column12: Mower County Sheriff's Office, Steele County Sheriff's Office, Freeborn County Sheriff's Office, Albert Lea Police Department, Faribault County Sheriff's Office
column15: Officers were dispatched to the 2100 block of 880th Avenue in Albert Lea at 7 p.m. on June 10 after receiving a report that 44-year-old Nathanial Bailey texted a woman that he had killed his mother. Bailey allegedly fled a traffic stop attempt by officers before arriving at his residence. He allegedly exited his vehicle with a handgun and multiple officers shot him.
column33: Katlynne Fisher, Sean Robbins, Darik Weigel, Sy Vanthavong

column15: According to a press release, a deputy responded to the 100 block of Eighth Street in Corydon for a family disturbance report Monday night. Officials say when the deputy arrived on scene, they encountered a man, later identified as Charles Powell Jr., with a machete. They say he was instructed to stop and drop the machete, but he refused and continued to approach the deputy. The deputy tased and then shot and killed him.

column7: Oakland Mills Rd and Carters Ln
column15: Howard County police received a call from a man in his 20s who reported that he had been repeatedly stabbed by a family member in a home in the 9200 block of Wilbur Court, according to the Howard County Police Department (HCPD). Just two minutes later, the 23-year-old man reportedly called 911 from the intersection of Oakland Mills Road and Carters Lane and said he was armed. Police allege the man approached an officer with a spear in his hand and they shot and killed him.

According to officials, officers were sent to the intersection of Hermitage and Lea Avenues at approximately 8:45 a.m. on Monday, June 9 to respond to reports of a man walking in the area while carrying a gun in his left hand. A MNPD spokesperson said Sgt. Robert Weaver, a 27-year veteran and community coordinator for the Hermitage precinct, responded to the call and saw the man walking along the sidewalk. He reportedly gave the man numerous commands, but the man did not comply and continued to walk away before turning around and charging toward Weaver with the gun in his hand. Weaver shot and killed him.

KSP was requested to respond to a disturbance at a residence west of Cynthiana on KY-36, where Ramon Morales, a 50, of Cynthiana, was unlawfully refusing to leave. Before a trooper arrived, Morales left the scene in a white Chevrolet van. Shortly after, a vehicle matching the description of the Morales vehicle had crashed into another car on KY-36 and was leaving the scene of that collision. Later that evening, a KSP trooper located Morales standing on the shoulder of the roadway in front of the residence of the earlier disturbance complaint. During the interaction with Morales, the trooper shot and killed him.

Preliminary information indicates the incident happened at approximately 10:38 on Sunday night on the 2000 block of N. Willow Avenue, where officers responded to serve a domestic assault warrant on Dawson McCracken. When officers arrived, McCracken was armed with a handgun. Law enforcement attempted to negotiate with him, but for reasons still under investigation, the situation escalated, McCracken pulled his gun, and officers fired several rounds striking McCracken.

Preliminary information indicates the shooting happened at around 10:19 p.m. Sunday on Highway 394 near Highway 11 West where a state trooper went to a crash. The trooper encountered the driver involved in the crash and, believing the person was inebriated, attempted to arrest him. For reasons still under investigation, the subject fled, and the situation escalated. “The subject produced a gun, and the trooper fired at the subject killing him,” according to the TBI statement.

Virginia State Police received a call about a suspicious situation along Highway 903 in Mecklenburg County. When police arrived on scene, a vehicle took off and a police chase was initiated. During the pursuit, officials said the man vehicle crashed in an open field and the man then pulled out a knife while reportedly refusing to comply with the trooper’s commands. They shot and killed him.

column7: 10th St W and W Ave J 12
column15: An LA County deputy shot and killed a man in response to a robbery call. The deputy was shot and injured.

Sheriff Mina said during a news conference that deputies responded to a home on North Ortman Drive around 3:30 p.m. in response to a man in a mental health crisis who was not taking his medication and was “acting erratically in the street and breaking things." According to Mina, deputies were in the hallway of the home for about five minutes trying to speak with the man when he “came out very violently” and within a second, tried to stab one of the deputies. “He then grabbed the deputy’s gun and tried to stab the deputy again. It’s at that point our deputy used his service weapon, striking the man several times," Mina said.

On June 7, 2025, at approximately 9:20pm, a Malheur County Sheriff’s Deputy responded to the Harper area for a disturbance/assault complaint between neighbors. The Deputy attempted to grab Mr. Reiter over a fence, but was shoved back by Mr. Reiter. The Deputy decided to use his department issued Taser to attempt and take Mr. Reiter into custody. One of the attempts was somewhat effective, and when Mr. Reiter was briefly on the ground the Deputy was able to get over the fence. Mr. Reiter recovered quickly and charged at the Deputy, shoving the Deputy to the ground and taking control of the Taser. The Deputy continued to make verbal commands for Mr. Reiter to get on the ground since he was under arrest (these commands had been given numerous times up to this point), but Mr. Reiter continued to refuse both verbally and physically. Mr. Reiter then tossed the Taser to the ground nearby. Mr. Reiter retrieved a large storage box out of a small trailer and began searching though it. The Deputy responded by again placing Mr. Reiter at gunpoint and ordering him to step away from the box and not to reach into it, making it very clear that if Mr. Reiter continued to do so the Deputy would have to shoot. More yelling followed, and Mr. Reiter then quickly reached into the container, pulled out a hammer and made a motion towards the Deputy. The Deputy responded by firing 5 rounds from his firearm, striking Mr. Reiter.

A man is believed to have killed his father-in-law and mother-in-law Friday morning before exiting the couple’s Adams County home armed with a knife in the area of Lofton Court and Kokai Circle near Sherrelwood Park. Adams County Sheriff’s deputies then shot the 51-year-old man after trying several methods to get him to drop the knife.

Williamson County Sheriff’s Office deputies responded to a 911 call reporting a man had forced entry into a residence on Drake Road at 9:58 a.m. June 6, 2025. According to the WCSO, the female occupant confronted the man who then fled into the woods. Police pursued the man and allege he pointed a gun at them. They shot and killed him.

Deputies were called to a report of a domestic disturbance at a home on Shockley Road in Scottsville, state police said in a news release. When they arrived they allege a man brandished a gun and they shot and killed him.

According to the Allegheny County Police Department, just before 4 a.m., officers with the Pittsburgh Bureau of Police were called to Carpenter Lane for a domestic disturbance, and one of the people involved was taken to court to file an emergency protection-from-abuse order. Then, just before 6 a.m., police returned to the home to serve the order. Officials said once police were inside, a man approached an officer with a knife and stabbed them. Another officer fired multiple shots, killing the man, authorities said.

At about 6:45 p.m. June 5, police went to a neighborhood near West Pershing Avenue and 87th Lane after receiving information about a possible kidnapping, according to a Peoria Police Department release. Preliminary information indicates a woman was pushing her child in a stroller while walking near a greenbelt. A man came up behind her and placed her in a bear hug. During the altercation, the man attempted to take the child but was unsuccessful, police said. The woman called her husband who was nearby, and he arrived and attempted to contact the suspect in a cul-de-sac north of West Pershing Avenue and 87th Lane. “Officers arrived on scene and contacted the male subject. The subject failed to comply with officer commands, which resulted in an officer-involved shooting. The officer fired at least one round at the subject, striking him,” the release stated.

According to the Mendocino County Sheriff's Office, deputies were called to the 2000 block of Hearst Willits Road near the town of Willits around 7 p.m. following reports of a fight between the hitchhiker and the driver. The California Highway Patrol and police from Willits also responded to the scene. As they attempted to arrest the man, deputies said they used pepper spray. The sheriff's office said he continued to resist and assaulted a deputy as they attempted to place handcuffs on him, prompting the use of a stun gun. The man was arrested and died soon thereafter.

Humboldt County Sheriff’s Office (HCSO) received a call reporting a male subject who had entered the Bear River Recreation Center with a bandaged, bloody arm and was actively dripping blood throughout the facility. HCSO deputies arrived on scene and determined that the subject was uncooperative but in need of medical attention. At approximately 3:30 p.m., HCSO deputies cleared the scene and the subject agreed to leave. However, instead of leaving, the subject became combative and confronted the deputies with a weapon in a threatening manner. An HCSO deputy discharged their service weapon at the man, striking the man.

One person is dead after a police shooting Thursday that followed a morning spent negotiating with a man police said was armed with a gun in the parking lot of nonprofit A Precious Child. Shortly after officers arrived, they noticed he had a gun, and called in the department’s Crisis Negotiating Team and its mental health Co-Response Team. They spent more than three hours negotiating with the man, then shot and killed him.

Deputies responded following multiple 911 calls about a woman trying to enter homes without permission. When law enforcement arrived, they found Harrison armed with a stick. She reportedly refused commands to drop the weapon and was tased, which appeared to have little effect. She was arrested and charged with obstruction of a law enforcement officer and public drunkenness. Harrison reportedly continued to be uncooperative and was placed in a holding cell. A short time later, she became unresponsive and died.

Rivera was an officer shot and killed by another officer. She was shot as officers were chasing a person who ran into an apartment. Another man then pointed a gun at the officers and officers shot and unintentionally killed Rivera.

The incident took place around 2:15 p.m. Thursday at a home on Fair Oaks Drive. Police were told a man was attacking members of the Dutchess County Mobile Crisis Team with a sword. At the scene, police entered the home and found one man with a head injury. The man was also located inside. Police said there was a confrontation between the man, who they said was armed, and responding officers. An officer fired shots from his department issued handgun during the confrontation, police said.

Officers were called around 7 p.m. to a home in the 3100 block of Cascades Court in Tyler. Dispatchers initially received the call as a suspicious person, but it was later updated to a disturbance involving a person inside a home. Erbaugh said when officers arrived, they entered the home and made contact with O’Kelly inside the home. “... I can’t go into the specifics there, but there was an officer-involved shooting at that point in time,” Erbaugh said.

A woman died Thursday after being shot by deputies during a narcotics search warrant at a residence in Brazoria County, according to Constable Precinct 1. The incident occurred shortly after 3 p.m., when Brazoria County Constable Precinct 1, with assistance from multiple local agencies, executed the search warrant at a residence in the county. During the operation, the person allegedly pointed a weapon at a deputy. In response, two Constable deputies discharged their firearms. CPR was immediately started, and EMS transported the suspect to a local hospital, where she was later pronounced dead.
Deputies pursued a man who allegedly was involved in drive by shootings. His vehicle was disabled using spike strips. They allege he fired at them and they shot and killed him.

column12: Indiana State Police, Clay County Sheriff's Office
column15: Trooper Caleb Cannon was requested to investigate a suspicious subject and vehicle near a residence in Cory, but the subject had left the area before Cannon arrived. A short time later, he observed a vehicle matching the description from the original call traveling eastbound on Clay County Road 300 South. Cannon observed the vehicle travel left of center. Cannon attempted a traffic stop, but the driver disregarded the emergency lights and continued traveling away, instigating a low-speed pursuit that headed south on County Road 300 toward Indiana 59. Police used stop sticks and then a PIT maneuver to cause the vehicle to crash. They recovered the man from the vehicle and he died a short time later.
Police shot and killed a man following a standoff. Few additional details are available.

Officers went to a private residence in the 5200 block of Evanbrook Terrace near the intersection of SE 59th and Bryant to execute an arrest warrant on 40-year-old Jose Martinez that was “sex-crimes related,” according to Knight. “During service of the search warrant, Jose Martinez armed himself with a gun and fled the residence on foot, into a wooded area,” said Knight in a follow-up press release Thursday. “Sgt. [Justin] Kuehn found Martinez, who had thrown his firearm over a fence and was attempting to retrieve it. Sgt. Kuehn ordered Martinez to stop. Martinez ignored Sgt. Kuehn’s commands, reached down and picked up the firearm, and was subsequently shot by Sgt. Kuehn.”

Garland police said officers responded to a disturbance around 1:50 p.m. at a Motel 6 in the 12700 block of LBJ Freeway. The call involved a dispute between a motel tenant and hotel management. When officers tried to speak with the tenant, later identified as Shawn Dylan Burt, 52, police said he pointed a firearm at them. Officers took cover, prompting a SWAT team response due to the threat of Burt, according to police. Police said detectives secured a warrant, and nearby motel rooms were evacuated for safety. SWAT negotiators attempted to contact Burt, who was barricaded, but received no response. After several unsuccessful attempts to communicate, police said officers deployed tear gas into the room. According to authorities, Burt confronted SWAT officers at the window with a gun, and one officer fired a rifle, striking him. Another person was found dead in the room.

Ronald Gainer Jr., had been involved in a domestic violence confrontation with his girlfriend, who left the apartment. Gainer allegedly walked out of the apartment and fired a shot into the air and at an adjacent apartment building, which prompted the call to police. Officers from the LAPD’s Olympic Division responded about 10 p.m. Tuesday to the shots fired call at the location in the 1000 block of Ardmore Avenue, near 11th Street, in the Harvard Heights area just south of Koreatown, and while there, Gainer allegedly exited the apartment again, “armed with a firearm,” prompting police to open fire, according to the LAPD. On Wednesday, California Attorney General Rob Bonta announced that the state Department of Justice is investigating the case under the authority of Assembly Bill 1506, which provides for state investigations into shootings of unarmed individuals.

Pueblo Police said officers responded to an alleged theft at Famous Footwear on the north side of Pueblo near I-25 and Dillon Drive around 1:23 p.m. When the man ran from the store, officers said they chased him on foot and by car. According to police, the man ran to the Colorado State Patrol headquarters at Wills and Outlook in Pueblo and pulled out a firearm. Police said they followed the man and ordered him several times to drop his weapon. Officers said the man did not comply with their orders, and that was when an officer struck the man with his vehicle.

column7: Boyles Mill Rd NE and River Rd NE
column12: Whitfield County Sheriff's Office, Dalton Police Department
column15: Preliminary information indicates that on June 3, 2025, at about 11:40 p.m., narcotics investigators with the Whitfield County Sheriff’s Office and the Dalton Police Department were conducting a narcotics investigation near Boyles Mill Road in Dalton, GA. At the conclusion of the investigation, investigators attempted to arrest Zuccarini. During the arrest, Zuccarini pointed a gun towards investigators. The investigators fired their guns, hitting Zuccarini.

At around 3:17 p.m., the officer attempted a traffic stop on a white Dodge Caravan in the area of Van Dyke Avenue and 22 Mile Road. During the stop, police say the suspect, a 41-year-old Troy man who was the sole occupant of the Caravan, exited the vehicle and ran away from the officer. Police say the officer chased the suspect behind a business in the area and gave commands to the suspect to stop before deploying a Taser. The suspect reportedly continued to run from the officer before ultimately allegedly drawing a weapon. The officer reportedly gave the suspect verbal commands to drop the weapon before firing and striking the man.

Deputies were serving an arrest warrant outside Sanger, near Bolivar, on June 3, according to a press release. They arrived at 10000 Field Lark Lane close to 2:45 p.m. Deputies contacted the man, 58-year-old Kenneth Wayne Jones. He drew a gun on the deputies, and they shot him.

A McKenzie County deputy is on administrative leave after being involved in an early morning shooting. Deputies responded to a suicidal male and allege the man pointed a firearm at them when they shot and killed him.

A Fulton County police officer on Sunday morning shot and killed a man who officials said charged at him with a piece of flat metal at an apartment complex in southwest Atlanta. At about 7:40 a.m., the GBI said the officer confronted a man who broke his patrol car’s window at Heritage Station Apartments on McDaniel Street. The officer handles security at the complex and a witness reported the damage to him, officials said.

According to police, officers responded to a call about a person jogging who had been shot in the leg near Eisenhower International School. "This is a sprawling scene that's taken place over multiple blocks," Tulsa Police Department's Capt. Richard Meulenberg said. "What had happened, which is very atypical and very unusual, we responded to a 'shots fired' call where a jogger said they were hit. Didn't know who shot them or why they were shot." While at that scene assisting the jogger, police said a man emerged from behind a responding fire truck. The man allegedly began firing at officers, then escaped in a car eastbound toward 56th Street and Harvard Avenue. Police chased the man until he stopped in a cul-de-sac near 58th Street and Delaware Place. Police allege the man fired at officers and they shot and killed him.

Officers responded to the 6400 block of Passo Via after a report of family violence.According to the El Paso Police Department, as officers approached the residence, Salvador Valdiviezo began firing a handgun. Both officers on the scene returned fire, and Valdiviezo was struck several times.

Officers initiated a traffic stop in the 3300 block of Dawes Road in reference to a male subject who had threatened to kill a known female in the 9000 block of Scott Dairy Loop Road S. a short time earlier. During the traffic stop, the 75-year-old subject produced a firearm and threatened to harm himself. Police allege the man pointed a gun at them and they shot and killed him.

San Diego Police Officers were dispatched to check the welfare of a male adult standing in the middle of the street blocking traffic on the 4400 block of Coronado Avenue, in the city of San Diego. The male was heard making suicidal statements. A San Diego Police Officer arrived, and the officer called for additional units to assist. The male entered a small black sedan, and a pursuit ensued through surface streets in Ocean Beach. The vehicle pursuit ended at the intersection of Ebers Street and Bermuda Avenue after the black sedan collided with a black Jeep driving in the intersection. The male got out of his vehicle and made suicidal statements. Less lethal options were utilized. The male while armed with a knife advanced on officers. One San Diego Police Officer shot and killed him.

column7: N Martin Luther King Jr Blvd and Goldmine Dr
column15: Officers tried to pull over Joshua Hayden Sikes, 18, on Old Charlotte Highway at Rocky River Road, but he kept going prompting a pursuit. Officers deployed stop sticks at Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard and Goldmine Rock, stopping the man's vehicle. They allege he shot an officer and fled on foot. Officers found Sikes who had a rifle. He shot at officers a second time. They returned fire killing Sikes.

The pursuit happened in the early morning hours of Friday, May 30 when California Highway Patrol officers attempted to pull over a driver in a silver Aston Martin for driving at speeds exceeding 70 mph, officials said. That driver, later identified as 30-year-old Martin Soria, sped away, leading officers on a chase that was eventually called off due to the dangerous speeds. An air unit continued to follow the car, directing officers to the crash site in the area of Washington Boulevard and Soto Street in Boyle Heights. After crashing into a utility pole, Soria ran for about a block before being apprehended. Officers used force against him, tackling him to the ground. He died at the scene.
Police responded to a shooting that did not involve Cornelius, a rapper. They released a K-9 against him, biting him. This caused an infection and severe organ failure, killing him.

According to the Taylorsville Police Department, the incident began at 9:30 p.m. when officers located the stolen vehicle being driven by 35-year-old Caysee Rebolloso. When officers attempted to stop Rebolloso, she fled the area. Officers decided not to pursue Rebolloso, instead using a Department of Public Safety helicopter to follow her before police used tire deflation devices along 500 West to stop the car. Rebolloso continued to drive until she crashed into two other vehicles at the intersection of 4800 South and 500 West. Rebolloso was taken to the hospital, where she died from her injuries.

Chicago police said tactical officers tried to stop a man in an alley in the 4300 block of West North Avenue. As officers approached, police said the man took off running into a backyard. Police said when officers caught up to him and tried to detain him, the man's gun went off, hitting the police officer in the leg. Police said the officer then fired back, hitting the man.

column12: St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department, Federal Bureau of Investigation
column15: According to Mitch McCoy, a spokesman for the St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department, the shooting happened around 11:40 a.m. in the 5600 block of Natural Bridge near Clara Avenue, located in the Mark Twain I-70 Industrial neighborhood. Just after 11 a.m., officers spotted a vehicle tied to a robbery investigation from earlier in the month. McCoy said officers attempted to pull the vehicle over, but the man sped off. St. Louis police and and members the FBI Fugitive Task Force were involved in the lengthy pursuit, which ended outside Shapiro Metal. The man jumped out of the vehicle and ran behind the scrapyard. Police and federal agents chased after the man and found him in some heavy brush near the railroad tracks behind the business. “Officers, along with other members of law enforcement, started searching that area. They located him, possibly hiding, gave verbal commands for him,” McCoy said. “At some point, shots were fired by law enforcement and officer fired shots along with a member of the FBI Fugitive Task Force.”

According to the preliminary investigation, at approximately 1:00 a.m., police officers from the Woodbridge Police Department were dispatched to a residence on East Tappen Street in the Port Reading section of Woodbridge, in response to a 911 call reporting a domestic dispute. Mr. Allen left the area of the residence on East Tappen Street and traveled on foot eastbound along Port Reading Avenue to a convenience store in Port Reading. During an encounter with Mr. Allen, who was holding a baseball bat, outside the store, Woodbridge Police Sergeant Marco Bruno fired his service weapon.

Albuquerque Police Chief Harold Medina says this incident began Tuesday when they tried arresting a man with parole violations. Police named that man as Jorge Eduardo Dominguez. But this saga reached a deadly end Wednesday night at the Comfort Suites by the Sunport when APD’s SWAT team approached Dominguez’s hotel room. That’s when police say he broke a window and jumped out of the building. Police unleashed their K-9, Rebel, who then latched onto Dominguez. That’s when Dominguez reportedly pulled out a gun and officers shot and killed him.

Greenville County Communications received an anonymous tip that the man wanted out of Spartanburg County was in the area of Cannon Road, which is outside of Greer. When Greenville County deputies arrived, they made contact with the armed man in the area of the 3000 block of Cannon Road, where a deputy-involved shooting occurred involving five GCSO deputies. Greenville County Sheriff Hobart Lewis posted a video to Facebook, saying, "At some point, the man came out with a weapon. The deputies on scene fired upon him, [and] he is deceased. The coroner is on the scene as well as SLED, conducting the external investigation into the event here today.”

column7: N Gary Rd and W Skyline Dr
column15: Deputies were called to a home for a "domestic disturbance." A man in his 20s was shot and killed by a single deputy. The man's name has not been released.

column7: SR 20/Canton Highway and Conference Center Drive
column12: Bartow County Sheriff's Office, Cartersville Police Department
column15: GBI says before the traffic stop, the woman, identified as 50-year-old Carrie Hall of Cartersville, “reportedly arrived at a home in Bartow County and fired a gun.” The homeowner, who said they knew Hall, identified her and gave her name to responding deputies. Around 8:40 p.m., deputies and a Cartersville police officer found the Hall’s vehicle and began a felony traffic stop. During the traffic stop, GBI says Hall “got out of the vehicle armed with a gun and did not comply with repeated verbal commands to drop the weapon.” They shot and killed her.

Dorsey was involved in a verbal argument with a roommate, had reportedly drank alcohol and left his residence on Robsion Road. An off-duty JPD officer, who the police chief identified Thursday as Ofc. Stevonte Wood, became aware of the disturbance involving Dorsey and authorities say he attempted to speak with him. Sanders said in a news conference Wood was not wearing his gear because he was at home with his kids when the neighbors called for him. The situation escalated when Dorsey stepped into Wood's front yard and approached his front door; Sanders said Wood gave clear commands for Dorsey to stop but he continued to "ignore commands and act aggressively, throwing garbage cans, breaking a storm door, smashing vehicle windows with his fists, attempting to break in multiple homes, and making threats of violence toward others in the area." Sanders said Dorsey charged at Wood before the officer fired his gun, fatally shooting him. The police chief confirmed Dorsey did not have a weapon on him.

Deputies from the Calhoun County Sheriff's Office were dispatched to a call of a possible shooting victim who appeared to be suicidal about 10:45 a.m. Wednesday, May 28, on 18 1/2 Mile Road in Marshall, according to the sheriff department. "Upon arrival, deputies encountered a 41-year-old Marshall man armed with what appeared to be a long rifle-style gun, which was pointed at a deputy. During the encounter, the individual was fatally shot. No deputies were injured," the sheriff's office said in a statement. It was a BB gun.

The incident unfolded on Wednesday, May 28, around 1 p.m. at a home on the 100 block of North 38th Street in South Whitehall Township. Police responded to the scene following a 911 call that reported a man with a gun. Responding South Whitehall Township police officers were then confronted by a man who was armed with what appeared to be a rifle, officials said. The officers repeatedly told the man to drop the weapon but he refused and continued walking towards them, according to investigators. The officers used less-than-lethal-force on the man but were unable to subdue him, officials said. The officers then fired around six shots, striking the man who was pronounced dead at the scene.

A man was killed and his girlfriend injured in an officer-involved shooting in Middletown on Tuesday morning. The incident occurred at a home on Garden Avenue, where police were serving a search warrant as part of a prolonged investigation into a narcotics trafficker. According to police, the man opened the door holding a gun when they arrived to serve the warrant. It is unclear if he fired any shots, but police did, resulting in the man's death at the scene. On Wednesday, the Butler County Coroner identified him as Michael Baker Junior, 47.

CCSO said the first deputy on scene reportedly found a “badly injured” 74-year-old woman lying on the living room floor. The lady reportedly told him a female family member had attacked and beaten her. After finding the suspect in a bedroom armed with a “sharp pointed object,” the deputy reportedly told her to drop it several times, with the suspect each time refusing. The Sheriff’s Office said the 34-year-old female suspect made a sudden movement toward the deputy, who then shot her in the upper body with his handgun.

column12: Corpus Christi Independent School District Police Department
column15: An off-duty Corpus Christi Independent School District police officer faces murder charges following a fatal shooting in Ingleside Monday morning that authorities say may be linked to a love triangle. Ashley Nicole Transmeier, 29, was arrested after Ingleside police responded to reports of gunshots at a home on Capehart Circle. Police have identified the victim as 54-year-old Albert Florencio Howie, an Ingleside resident.

column7: Judith St and Hudson Ave S
column15: Family told KSL TV that Christy Allen had called 911 to report that her estranged husband, Christian Allen, whom she had recently filed a protective order against, had broken into their home. Christy Allen and her two teenage sons hid inside a bedroom while they waited for police to arrive. Once they did, police won’t say what happened further, except that two officers shot and killed Christian Allen.

Sheriff Grady Judd says Polk County deputies shot and killed an armed man who was attacked by an alligator while swimming across a lake, then charged at the deputies with a pair of garden shears before trying to grab a gun from a patrol vehicle.

An officer with the Bloomfield Police Department was injured and the man was killed in a shootout that took place at around 10:55 p.m. Monday, May 26. According to Bloomfield police, the man allegedly opened fire on an officer during a traffic stop near Jordan Street. A fellow officer returned fire, shooting and killing the man.

A man was fatally shot by police in Fontana after allegedly pointing a gun at officers responding to a domestic dispute. The incident occurred Sunday morning in the 9100 block of Date Avenue, where officers were dispatched to an apartment. According to Fontana police, the man aimed a firearm at officers as the apartment door was opened, leading officers to fire their weapons.

According to Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office Chief Deputy Joseph Maurer, the agency received a burglary call at 4:41 a.m. at the 7500 block of Carlton Circle. When deputies were on scene, they were informed that a grandmother, Rosamond Brookins, 46, had shot her daughter. Deputies allege Brookins raised a firearm at them and they shot and killed her.

The chase started the chain of events around 9:30 a.m. when deputies attempted to stop the motorcycle for a registration violation on U.S. 421 just north of Clinton. According to Smith, a pursuit ensued onto several county secondary roads and eventually back to U.S. 421 near Kitty Fork Road. During the pursuit, the captain said, deputies noticed that the motorcycle operator had a firearm on his side. When the motorcycle driver approached Kitty Fork, Smith said, the operator lost control of the bike and crashed. At that point, reports note that the motorcycle operator drew his weapon and a deputy fired their service revolver, striking the man.

A man who police say was threatening officers with a bat and a chunk of concrete was shot and killed in Houston's Spring Branch area Friday afternoon. According to Houston Police, the fatal shooting happened at the corner of Wirt and Hammerly after a Taser was ineffective, police said.

column12: Unified Police Department of Greater Salt Lake
column15: Officers responded to reports of an armed robbery near the 160 West and 7200 South just after 2 a.m. on Friday, May 23. They shot and killed someone, but few details are available.

The incident began Thursday morning when police were called to a shooting and armed robbery of a vehicle. An individual had been shot and taken to the hospital for treatment. Police were notified that the person fled the scene in the victim's vehicle. The vehicle was located on Upper Wetumpka Road, where state and local law enforcement attempted a traffic stop. The driver, Raymond Tellis Jr., 19, of Montgomery, resisted arrest and allegedly pulled a firearm from his waistband. A special agent with ALEA's State Bureau of Investigation fired at Tellis, fatally wounding him.

A 19-year-old Somalian refugee died after a Douglas County Sheriff’s deputy fired into a vehicle in North Omaha early Thursday. Janidi Ibrahim died after shots were fired into an SUV near 48th and Pratt streets, not far from Fontenelle Park. The sheriff’s office later confirmed that the deputy was part of the Special Operations Group and was conducting a firearms investigation. As the deputy made contact with the vehicle around 2:30 a.m. Thursday, authorities said some people inside the vehicle ran from the scene but that Ibrahim stayed in the driver’s seat, where he was hit by the gunfire.

BPD says that at 5:45 p.m., the man reportedly tried to stab an officer outside the home improvement store. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation (TBI), which was called to look into the deadly shooting, says the officers were in the area taking a report on a shoplifting, and that the man with the knife was one of at least two accused thieves they were looking for.

The incident occurred around 8:08 p.m. in the 200 block of South Second Street after El Centro police responded to a call regarding a suspicious individual reportedly attempting to burglarize a residence. The caller informed dispatchers that the individual, described as an adult male, was believed to be armed with a firearm, police stated. An officer made contact with the subject, and during the encounter, an officer-involved shooting occurred. The person was pronounced deceased at the scene.

Police responded to a domestic violence incident. Police say that the person refused to leave the home and was holding a knife. When the person allegedly refused to drop his weapon or leave the home, an officer fired a 40 mm less-lethal round. The person then went back into the home, and officers entered the home to arrest the person. A second officer fired a 40 mm less-lethal round and when the person moved towards police, a third officer fired a gun and hit the suspect. As the suspect tried to get up, a fourth officer discharged a Taser. Police provided medical aid and an ambulance brought the suspect to Mercy Hospital where he later died.
column33: Timothy Morin, Steve Minion, Michael Blair, Emily Giese

column15: According to First Deputy Commissioner John Stanford, officers were conducting a "pedestrian investigation" at Mutter and Somerset streets around 6:30 p.m. "As they were approaching, a scuffle ensued with the male and the officers, at which point in time, the male produced a handgun from a bag that he was carrying on his person," said Stanford. At some point, police say the man's gun discharged, and that's when two officers opened fire, hitting the man in the torso.

During a news conference Wednesday, Lott played audio from a 911 call in the area from a resident saying they saw two people walking around checking cars at an apartment complex. The caller said he saw two men, one wearing black and the other wearing red. Shortly after, the caller states he heard gunshots. The bodycam video shows a deputy running into the entrance of the complex and chasing a person before deploying a K-9. Investigators said deputies were able to find the two people, 20-year-old Degeorge Darby and 20-year-old John Williams. Both took off running according to Lott and but Williams quickly surrendered. Investigators told reporters Wednesday that Darby continued running before he rounded a corner and began shooting at a deputy and his canine. The deputy was identified as Richard Jeffcoat. Deputies shot and killed him.

Police were called to a disturbance on Ridgewood Circle around 9:15 p.m. after receiving reports that a woman had been shot. Police state that when officers arrived, they were confronted by a man outside the residence who allegedly fired at them, police said. An officer shot and killed the man. The person in this incident has been identified as Juan Jose Rivera-Robles, a 37-year-old resident from Plano.

A Utah Highway Patrol trooper was patrolling eastbound I-70 near milepost 30. The trooper noticed a vehicle come up behind him at more than 90 miles per hour and activated his emergency lights, but said the person's vehicle fled at more than 140 miles per hour. Police used spike strips against the vehicle, causing it to crash and the driver to be ejected. He was killed.

Police responded to a reported domestic violence situation. Columbus Division of Police Sgt. Joe Albert said over the next hour he was able to make contact with the man over the phone and with the assistance of negotiators attempted to deescalate the incident. The suspect continued to fire shots at SWAT officers on multiple occasions. “He fired out of the residence multiple times at SWAT officers at the scene. At their equipment, at the SWAT officers who were outside of the residence,” Albert said. “So, this male was very violent. Had no regard for the police at scene here. Was obviously attempting to harm multiple police officers here at scene.”

Mohave County Sheriff’s Office Deputies responded to a home in the 1600 block of Smoketree Avenue to follow up with a domestic violence incident that had occurred in Topock the night before. The man, Case Taylor Chrouser, 38 of Topock, was wanted for several felony charges including aggravated assault by domestic violence, theft of a firearm and more. After deputies confirmed Chrouser was there, SWAT teams with the Mohave County Sheriff’s Office and Lake Havasu City Police Department began attempting negotiations. They say Chrouser did not respond to any negotiation attempts. By using a camera, authorities were able to see inside the bathroom, and they say Chrouser was pointing a gun towards the door. After giving him several verbal commands without a response, deputies say Chrouser opened the door and began firing the gun at the SWAT team. Three SWAT members with the Mohave County Sheriff’s Office returned fire and hit Chrouser. Medical crews began life-saving measures. However, Chrouser died from his injuries at the scene.

“The individual was reportedly armed with a firearm and attempted to jump inside of another individual’s car. At that point in time, our officers responding were able to locate the man and one of our officers did discharge a weapon,” said Cpl. Chris Bordelon.

On Sunday May 18, 2025 at approximately 7:30 p.m., officers from the Dundalk Precinct responded to the 8200 block of N. Boundary Rd., 21222 for a subject experiencing a mental health episode. Officers made contact with the armed subject to the rear of the residence. During this encounter, the officer responded to the actions of the armed subject, resulting in one officer discharging their firearm striking the adult male. The subject was transported to a local hospital and was later pronounced deceased. A firearm was recovered from the scene. The Independent Investigations Division with the Office of the Attorney General is investigating this matter.

Police responded to a car crash where a driver fled from the scene. At least four officers arrived at the crash and located the Fenton man a short distance from the site. Those officers shot and killed the Fenton man, who was armed with a handgun, Gibbons said. It’s unclear if the armed man pointed his weapon at police. Gibbons said a handgun was recovered at the scene.

Officers were dispatched to a crash on the freeway in the 10300 block of the North Freeway and learned that there had been a minor vehicle crash involving three vehicles. Two of the vehicles remained on the scene however a third vehicle had fled the location. Officers then moved the crash off the freeway and put a general broadcast over the radio for the possible third vehicle – a green SUV. Additional Northbelt patrol officers were able to locate the green SUV vehicle in the area and officers made contact with the driver. As the officers attempted to detain the driver of the green SUV for the crash investigation, the driver lifted his shirt up, reached for a visible gun in his waistband and pulled out the weapon. Two HPD officers then discharged their duty weapons more than once, striking the man.

column7: W William Cannon Dr and Cannonleague Dr
column15: A man in a wheelchair who was blocking traffic was shot and killed by an Austin police officer after he allegedly pointed a BB gun at the officer in South Austin on Saturday morning.

Washington State Patrol attempted to pull over a man on a motorcycle reported to be stolen near milepost 224 on northbound I-5, according to a May 18 news release from the Snohomish County Multiple Agency Response Team (SMART). The driver did not pull over, the release stated, and WSP pursued the man. The man abandoned the motorcycle at Alger Cain Lake Road, ran on foot to Camp 2 Road, then took a small boat onto Cain Lake. The 72-acre lake, which is about 9 miles southeast of Bellingham, near Alger, is surrounded by residential homes. While in the boat, the man “began firing rounds from a handgun in multiple directions,” according to the release. Whatcom County’s SWAT team responded to the incident. Officers shot the man while he was in the boat.

Troopers received a report of a reckless driver near the 7-mile marker eastbound on Interstate 40 near Van Buren, the release states. Troopers suspected this vehicle was connected to an earlier domestic disturbance and aggravated robbery in Fort Smith. The man stopped at the Hilltop Travel Center in Alma and entered the store. Troopers and Crawford County deputies responded to the scene, according to the release, and an altercation occurred between the man and law enforcement, during which the suspect produced a handgun and fled. Officers pursued the man, repeatedly commanding him to drop his weapon, the release states. The man faced the officers while still armed, and refused to comply with their commands. Troopers fired their weapons, fatally striking the man.

Officers were initially responding to reports of an assault with a deadly weapon. Police say that upon arrival to the multi-unit property they were directed by witnesses to a pathway between the units, where the man, 23-year-old Jose Gonzalez Ramos, had allegedly stabbed his wife multiple time. "There, they encountered Ramos, who was advancing towards the officers with a knife raised in his right hand, resulting in an Officer-Involved Shooting ... and the deployment of a 40mm less lethal launcher," LAPD said in a statement on Saturday. "Ramos was struck by gunfire and fell to the ground, where he was taken into custody."

In a release, deputies said that the SWAT team served a search warrant in a drug case at the home around 2:20 p.m., located at 5614 Lejune Drive. But as the SWAT team entered and tried to clear the area of danger, they ran into a man in a bedroom, who reached behind a door where a rifle was located, deputies added. Per investigators, a deputy then fired on the man, who was struck and later taken to the hospital. He died just before 3 p.m.

Deputy attempted to pull over a Jeep driven by Ronald Evans near a recreational complex. Sills said Evans was driving slowly, was not wearing a seatbelt, and appeared to be under the influence of alcohol. When the deputy asked for his driver’s license, Evans fled the scene, prompting a pursuit. The chase ended when Evans made a sudden turn into the C & J Store parking lot. He then exited the vehicle and pointed a firearm at the deputy, Sills said. The deputy fired multiple shots.

column7: Lodge Service Dr and Wyoming Ave
column15: Michigan State Police Director Colonel James F. Grady II said the Trooper initiated the traffic stop after noticing a violation. Officials said during the encounter, a physical altercation occurred between the Trooper and the man, who was a 41-year-old man out of Highland Park, leading to the man firing multiple shots at the Trooper. The Trooper was struck three times: two rounds hit his vest, and one round struck his shoulder. In response, the Trooper returned fire, hitting the 41-year-old man, who succumbed to his injuries at the scene.

According to a news release, officers responded to reports of multiple shots being fired at the athletic club, shortly after 1:30 p.m. Officers responded to the scene and identified a suspect standing at the door armed with a firearm, Boveda said. The suspect then ran out the door, and officers discharged their firearms striking him.
column33: Kaid Urban, Skeeter Black, Aaron Javier

column15: Chattanooga Police Chief John Chambers says officers were patrolling outside of the mall when they noticed a person acting in a “suspicious manner”. He says after they developed probable cause to conduct a traffic stop, that suspect fled from them and a pursuit initiated. Chief Chambers says speeds in the chase reached over 100 miles per hour despite the chase remaining in the mall’s parking lot and the ring road surrounding the mall. He says the man began crashing into other vehicles, and then near the Olive Garden on Hamilton Place Boulevard, attempted to ram into officers. That’s when officers fired upon that man, killing him.

It all started last Friday when authorities responded to a report of a robbery in the 5100 block of Almeda Road.  Authorities said they later learned a man, later identified as Harrison, stole merchandise and displayed a large knife when he was confronted by store employees. Officials stated when officers arrived, they located a man matching Harrison's description and gave him verbal commands to stop. However, Harrison advanced toward one of the officers with a machete. The officer, identified as Officer L. Jumonji, shot and killed Harrison.

HPD patrol officers responded to a call about a suicidal individual at an apartment complex at the above address. Officers located the apartment where the call came from and were met by a female who stated she called regarding her brother. At that moment, a male appeared behind the female and suddenly charged out of the apartment with a large knife in his hand. He ran directly toward the officers who were just outside the doorway. The officers began to retreat, but the male continued to advance. Police shot and killed him.

column12: South San Francisco Police Department, San Bruno Police Department
column15: Officers were called to the 300 block of Oyster Point Boulevard for a report of a man who was yelling obscenities and trying to use a metal object to force his way into a public restroom, the South San Francisco Police Department said in a statement. Officers arrived to find the man still breaking into the bathroom. He refused to identify himself and ran away with what appeared to be a gun in his hand, police said. Police said officers pursued the man and tried to subdue him using less-lethal force, but it was not effective. “The man then pointed the firearm at officers,” police said. “In response to the imminent threat, two officers from the South San Francisco Police Department and one officer from the San Bruno Police Department discharged their service weapons.” It was a replica firearm.

According to the 19th Judicial Critical Incident Response Team (CIRT), the Greeley Police Department received "numerous" calls about a man brandishing a knife in the 500 block of 16th Avenue. CIRT officials said an officer found the man "swinging a knife aggressively at passing cars" in the 1900 block of 2nd Street. The man reportedly did not comply with the officer's commands to drop the knife. According to the CIRT, the man "walked quickly towards the officer" and continued to not comply with commands when the officer discharged their firearm.

According to authorities, police were executing a search warrant for narcotics at the home at the time. They said troopers announced themselves and were confronted by a man armed with a shotgun. Police ordered the man to drop his weapon, but he refused and was shot by a trooper, officials said. They also shot a woman but non-fatally.

A man was shot and killed by Jacksonville Sheriff's Office SWAT officers early Wednesday after the agency says the man did not comply with officers' commands and alarmed neighbors by shooting a gun about 8-10 times at a home on the Westside before police showed up.

column15: According to the preliminary investigation, officers approached the man, who ran from the scene. Three officers chased him on foot, while another officer followed him in a car, according to the Attorney General’s Office. During the chase, officials said the man displayed a gun. Officers gave verbal commands, but the man did not comply, according to the investigation. Police said the chase ended with an exchange of gunfire between officers and the man. The man was shot and wounded, and officers provided medical aid until EMS arrived. The man was later pronounced dead at an area hospital, officials said.
column33: Enger Jimenez, Steven Foster, Tony Tiburzi

column15: Officers responded to the 200 block of North Townsend Street around 10 p.m. on Tuesday for a report of shots fired. The department said officers entered the building and Hogan was "actively shooting." Police exchanged gunfire with him. He was pronounced dead.

Police fatally shot a 25-year-old man Tuesday afternoon inside a Brownsville apartment after he allegedly brandished a knife and advanced toward officers who were responding to a domestic dispute, police said.

Officers had pulled over the Chevrolet Equinox SUV for a headlight issue. The driver had a female passenger in the car. Barraza said officers asked the driver if he had any weapons in the vehicle. He told them he didn’t. “One of the officers opened the passenger door, saw a gun on the man's lap,” Barraza said. “They had then gave him commands to put his hands up, to not touch the gun. He obviously did not react to the commands, and our officers then shot.”

As FPD officers arrived in the area, 36-year-old Fairbanks resident Thomas Bean began shooting at FPD officers with a semi-automatic rifle, striking the officers’ vehicles. FPD officers and Bean exchanged gunfire. Bean was struck by the FPD’s officers’ gunfire. Multiple Alaska State Troopers and additional FPD officers responded to assist. Bean continued to defy officer commands. Due to his actions, multiple law enforcement officers shot at Bean fatally striking him.

The officer was injured while Aurora Police Chief Todd Chamberlain said he was trying to deal with a combative person. The person, a male, was shot by police and declared dead sometime afterwards.

Police Chief Cal Green told 16 WAPT that officers were trying to serve a warrant after spotting a man allegedly involved in an attempted murder that happened last week. She said Stokes, 19, fired shots at officers, who returned fire, critically wounding the man.

According to Lehigh County District Attorney Gavin P. Holihan, officers were called to the Weis Market at 1500 N. Cedar Crest Blvd. after Vanbilliard began acting erratically. Witnesses and officers reported that he appeared paranoid and agitated, claiming that responding police were not “real officers” and were sent to kill him. Over several minutes, officers attempted to calm Vanbilliard, but his behavior escalated. His speech became disjointed and untethered to reality, authorities said. He began destroying items in the store and threw a wine bottle at officers. Police used a taser in an effort to subdue him. Despite the shock, Vanbilliard continued to physically resist. Officers eventually handcuffed him, after which he became unresponsive.

According to Pennsylvania State Police, Erie County 911 received several calls about a man smashing out a car window with a hammer, along with an additional call stating that someone was trying to attack their girlfriend with a hammer. Millcreek police responded to the incident, where they found a man matching the description from the callers. Police identified the man as 36-year-old Patrick Kanonczyk. A brief exchange occurred after which point shots were fired by Millcreek police officers at Kanonczyk, striking him.

Metro Nashville Police Department have been searching for Tadarius Milan Hunt, 29, since Sunday afternoon. Hunt, 29, was wanted on attempted criminal homicide for allegedly opening fire on the employee who barred Hunt from the property earlier that day, MNPD reported. Police say Hunt produced a semi-auto pistol at law enforcement when he was directed to stop and "an exchange of gunfire" occurred, resulting in Hunt's death. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation reports Hunt fired several shots at officers, and at least two officers returned fire.

SPD says Jack and his family were having an early Mother’s Day celebration when the incident happened. After officers arrived to the scene, they say the person came outside armed. The person was later fatally shot by police.

Officials first responded to the scene around 9:30 p.m. on Saturday, May 10, after receiving reports of domestic violence. The woman was reportedly carrying a handgun when she answered the door. “Deputies ordered her to drop the weapon,” the Duchesne County Sheriff’s Office said on Monday. “The person raised the handgun and pointing it at the deputy. The deputy fired at her striking her in the chest.”

Mohave County Sheriff’s Office Deputies responded to the area of Ty Street and College Drive for reports of a man pouring gasoline inside a home. The man was also armed, according to deputies. He refused to exit the house, which is when the SWAT team was called out to the scene. Deputies say the man was given commands to leave the house, but he was not complying. When the man finally came out of the house, deputies say he pointed a weapon at the SWAT team from MCSO and the Bullhead City Police Department. Deputies say that’s when SWAT members shot the man.

According to the St. Louis Metropolitan Police, at around 4:20 a.m. Friday, officers received a ShotSpotter notification in the 5100 block of Wells, where they then found a man dead with gunshot wounds on the porch of a home. Officers stayed in the area while waiting to acquire a search warrant. Police requested officers from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives to assist in the search for ballistic material, as the house had tall grass. At around 7 a.m., police said a man exited the home and talked to a homicide detective and a special agent before reentering the home, and then exiting again with a rifle. Police said he then began to shoot at officers, and one officer and one agent shot back, before he returned inside the home.

column15: OHP helped Cushing Police with a vehicle pursuit around 1:26 a.m. Officials say as the pursuit ended, the person began firing shots at law enforcement. Officers returned fire, fatally shooting the person.
Deputies responded to a call about a woman running around with a gun threatening someone. They allege she pointed a gun at them and they shot and killed her.

According to CPD, 4th District officers responded to a person with a gun call in the 13400 block of South Baltimore Avenue around 5:50 p.m. Thursday, for an individual wanted for an aggravated battery. Upon arrival, officers witnessed the person enter a vehicle and flee from the area. A short time later, the person then crashed his vehicle at Dearborn and Gostlin Street in Hammond, Indiana. They allege the person fired at them and they shot and killed the person.

A member of the NC State Highway Patrol conducted a traffic stop of a pickup truck on Interstate 85 southbound near mile marker 185 near Durham. Brown continued to flee and took the ramp to Red Mill Road, where he lost control and collided with an embankment. The incident took place near the 1900 block of Northeast Second Street yesterday evening. According to Local10, the woman was carrying a firearm inside a restaurant in the area before being confronted by deputies. They shot and killed her after she "presented a threat."

A woman was fatally shot Wednesday night by Orange County deputy sheriffs after she attacked them with a knife in an apartment as they responded to a report of someone being “battered and strangled,” according to the Sheriff’s Office.

Two people are dead after reportedly being shot by U.S. Marshals, who were serving a warrant on wanted individual. Officers gave orders for the man to drop the weapon, but he did not comply, according to the Poulsbo Police Department (PPD). PPD said officers attempted to "de-escalate and use non-lethal options," but their efforts were unsuccessful. The driver, now identified as Jemmie Earl Hicks Jr., 33, of Midway, reportedly refused to stop, prompting a police pursuit. The chase ended on Bullock County 106 near Flower Garden Road where investigators say he got out of his vehicle and ran into the nearby woods. “Subsequently, the foot pursuit led into a deadly force encounter between Hicks and the ALEA Trooper,” ALEA said in a statement. “Over the course of the incident, Hicks was injured by gunfire and the Trooper immediately rendered first aid.” Hicks died on the scene.
Police pulled over a man who had an active warrant. They allege the man shot at officers and they shot and killed him.

column15: Two deputies from the Sheriff’s Needles Station responded to a reported vehicle burglary and located a male, later identified as Michael Ray Richard, II, walking in the area. While deputies were detaining Richard, he pulled away and ran. Deputies pursued Richard on foot. Richard jumped over walls and returned back to the patrol units, where he retrieved a bag he had been carrying at the time of his detainment. The deputies caught up with Richard, who was armed with a handgun. Richard struggled with the deputies and fired the gun. A lethal force encounter occurred, and Richard was struck by gunfire.

Two officers from the South County Precinct arrived at the residence to arrest an adult male they were investigating for a first-degree harassment charge. The officer encounter then became deadly. Police shot and killed him after he allegedly displayed a firearm.

Harrisburg Police Department and Arkansas State Police joined in on the chase. The chase ended when a state trooper performed a tactical vehicle intervention on Interstate 555 near the 3-mile marker. The man, 54-year-old Joe Versie of Jonesboro, remained in the vehicle, ignoring commands from officers. Versie told officers that ”he had a weapon," and as he reached into the car, law enforcement fired their weapons and killed Versie.

Chandler police say multiple witnesses called 911 around 12:15 p.m. to report that an elderly neighbor was asking for help after getting into an argument with a family member. Witnesses also told police that the man, only identified as a 27-year-old, was allegedly armed with a knife and had made suicidal and threatening statements toward the family member. When officers arrived, they allegedly told the man to drop the weapon and he did not comply. At some point, police say the man ran toward an officer with a knife in his hand. That is when the shooting happened.

The department had received multiple reports of a man armed with a handgun in the alley behind the school. Upon arrival, officers contacted the man and saw he had a handgun in his hand. They demanded that he dropped the weapon, but he refused and eventually made "a move that put the officers in fear of being shot themselves," according to Thomas. He had a replica firearm, not a real gun.

Once they arrived at the rear driveway of the hospital, one of the officers opened the transport vehicle's rear doors and began explaining the self-committal process to Rainey, according to officials. During this time, police say Rainey "became upset and quickly became agitated." Then, "without warning," police say Rainey rushed toward one of the officers, knocking him to the ground and a physical altercation ensued between all three. Police allege the man grabbed the officer's gun and they shot and killed him.

Chief Clay Morris said the response followed a report of a man armed with a hatchet and making threats of violence. “The man refused to comply with the officers' demands,‘’ Murray said. ”The man charged at officers while armed with a hatchet forcing an officer to discharge his firearm."

column15: Geneva when an officer approached a suspicious vehicle in a parking lot at 1500 South Randall Road. Pinehurst Police Deputy Chief Ken Hall said officers responded around 7:15 a.m. Wednesday to a report of a suspicious male at 11 Remington Lane. It was then, Hall said, that a man, later identified by the State Bureau of Investigation as Sawyer Felton Frye, 37, came out the front door, retrieved a firefighter’s axe near the entryway, and charged toward officers. Police shot and killed him.

Lockland police say they were called to assist in locating multiple people who had fled from the pursuit. Officials say one person had been located and taken into custody when a Lockland officer located another person walking along I-75, near mile post 14. Authorities say the officer reported the person had something in his hands and refused to obey commands. Officials say the officer attempted to use non-lethal force, using a taser and then shooting and killing the man.

Video from outside the precinct lot shows the man driving this vehicle up to a Home Depot parking space outside the precinct’s north/west lot. He is seen getting out and climbing the fence to get into the lot, where department vehicles are kept. From there, the SPD edited video switches to officers’ body-worn cameras, as they encounter the man, tell him to leave the lot; he walks away from them for a while, even up to a gate, then turns to face their way. They repeatedly tell him to drop the knife; then he starts moving toward them, picking up speed at one point, and that’s when one officer apparently fires a “less than lethal” weapon shortly before another fires his gun.

Modesto police shot and killed a man who was wanted on several warrants near a nutritional store. Few details are available about this shooting.

The caller said that he was sitting in the parking lot when an unknown male subject then approached his vehicle, made a comment about drug usage and brandished a firearm. As troopers arrived, George put on body armor and armed himself with an assault rifle, according to the troopers' report. He left in his car, and the victims were able to escape the residence. A Wasilla police officer stopped George in a traffic stop half a mile away from the residence. However, George fled in the vehicle, and the officer pursued him, according to troopers. George stopped at the intersection of Knik Goose Bay Road and Settlers Bay Drive, where he then got out of his vehicle and fired the assault rifle at the marked Wasilla police car. The Wasilla police officer returned fire, striking George. George was declared dead at the scene.

Kentucky State Police say Christian County Sheriff’s deputies were called for a disturbance, and when deputies arrived, 39-year-old Patrick Martinez fired shots at them, and they returned fire, hitting and killing Martinez.

The incident started after police said they received a call from a person in an apartment who reported a man with a "gun" sleeping on the floor. The man eventually woke up and left the apartment, using the caller as a "human shield." The victim broke away and the man allegedly pointed a BB gun at police and both officers shot and killed him.

According to the San Antonio Police Department, Officer Orlando Jimenez exited his patrol vehicle and approached a stopped vehicle during a traffic stop. The driver, identified as Miguel Morin, escaped through the passenger door and attempted to flee the scene, jumping over fences to escape. A man called 911 saying his brother had swung a knife at his father. Officers arrived on scene and found the man outside the home on the sidewalk. "The male was given several commands by officers, however, was uncooperative with the commands given to him," said police in a statement. At one point, the man abruptly lifted his shirt and removed a pellet gun. Police shot and killed him.

Lucrisia continued firing at officers, and one officer returned fire.”

Freddie Ware, 43, of Dallas, allegedly shot a woman before McKinney police arrived around 2:45 p.m. Thursday at the Red Roof Inn on Highway 75 (1300 North Central Expressway). According to police, Ware barricaded himself in a room. Police deployed a K-9 against him and then shot and killed him when he "presented a firearm."

The incident began on March 12 when Hayward officers responded to a reported disturbance involving a 41-year-old man at a residence on Virginia Street. According to police, the man, identified as Nathan Hoang, threw a brick through a window and confronted residents during a dispute. Officers say he later produced a screwdriver and adopted what they described as an “aggressive stance.” Police attempted to subdue Hoang using a stun device multiple times. After he was handcuffed and placed on a gurney, a paramedic from Falck — the private ambulance company serving the area — administered midazolam, a benzodiazepine commonly used for sedation in prehospital settings, according to The Mercury News. According to court records, Hoang stated he couldn’t breathe approximately 8 minutes after receiving the medication and soon became unresponsive. He was transported by ambulance to Eden Medical Center, where he was later declared brain dead.

Deputies with the Elbert County Sheriff's Office were called to a disturbance at a location off County Road 77 about 6:30 p.m. Wednesday. When deputies arrived, they found the man in a fifth wheel trailer where they tried to get him to come out unarmed. At first, deputies said he was armed with a handgun and refused requests to put down the gun. They said he went back inside the trailer but as he did, deputies shot him with "less lethal rounds" and the man retreated into his trailer. According to Elbert County investigators, the man complained about pain in his back from being struck with the less lethal round and negotiators worked with deputies to get him to come out peacefully. They said he refused. That's when deputies shot some pepper ball rounds into the trailer through the window and the man allegedly fired at least two rounds toward the deputies. They shot and killed him.

Police Department. Police say officers broke down the door and two of them fired their weapons, hitting the man.

Deputies shot Johnston after he allegedly fired a gun at them following hours of negotiation outside the home on Old Hwy. 21. They had initially responded to reports of a man with a gun behaving erratically.

According to preliminary information, the person pulled into a driveway in the 9000 block of Peavine Road, exited the vehicle, and fired at the officer. The driver reportedly advanced toward the officer on foot, after which the officer returned fire, striking and killing him.

At some point during the pursuit, deputies lost sight of the person's vehicle. Shortly after, they found the vehicle engulfed in flames. As deputies arrived at the scene of the fire, they reported hearing multiple gunshots. Law enforcement then located the person, who was armed with a 9 mm pistol. ACSO stated that the person pointed the weapon at one of the deputies and they shot and killed him.
Orlando police shot and killed a man allegedly holding an AR-15 in an open room, after responding to a call about a man with a gun.

An off-duty Boston police officer was inside the restaurant on Boylston Street around 5:30 p.m. when two people ran into the restaurant, pursued by a man armed with a knife.
